title: Benchmarking gastrointestinal involvement in systemic sclerosis: practical insights and unmet needs from a tertiary referral centre.
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) involvement is almost universal in patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc). Our aim was to benchmark and describe GI involvement in SSc, exploring potential clinical associations including in patients with myositis overlap. Retrospective, cross-sectional study. Patients attending a UK tertiary referral centre for SSc in 2024. Adult (n=149) patients with an established clinical diagnosis of SSc (excluding a very early diagnosis of SSc). Subgroup analysis of those with myositis overlap. None; observational study design, including description of prescribed treatments. Relevant patient and disease-related data were obtained from electronic patient record review. We developed a simple clinician-assessed score to assess GI symptoms burden: 0 ('none'), 1 ('effectively managed') or 2 ('unmanaged'). Descriptive statistics and appropriate testing were used to describe the data. We included 149 patients (female, 86%), most (71%) had limited cutaneous SSc and 13% had myositis. Median (IQR) SSc-disease duration was 11.1 (43.0) years. Over half (61%) had current GI symptoms (score 1 or 2); 43% had unmanaged symptoms (score 2). The most common symptoms were reflux (32%) and dysphagia (28%). Proton pump inhibitor use was high (81%). Both anticentromere (p=<0.001) and anti-Scl70 (p=0.01) antibodies were associated with GI symptoms, but not anti-RNA polymerase (p=0.78). No statistically significant association was seen between GI involvement and interstitial lung disease (p=0.06), pulmonary hypertension (p=0.42) or digital ulcers (p=0.84). No association was observed between GI involvement and disease duration (p=0.44). Over half (63%) with myositis overlap had GI involvement. GI involvement is common and often symptomatic in SSc, but not over-represented in patients with myositis overlap. Research is needed to understand natural history, pathobiology and heterogeneity, including early intervention strategies. NCA reference: 25HIP20.

title: A Biomolecular Sandwich Assay to Characterize the Binding Properties of Antisense Oligonucleotide Conjugates.
abstract: Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) are a treatment modality for genetic diseases, binding to ribonucleic acid (RNA) with high specificity, with downstream effects that eventually reduce, restore, or modify protein expression through distinct mechanisms. Conjugating ASOs to targeting ligands has emerged as a promising strategy to improve tissue-specific delivery, but there remains a lack of binding assays to study this class of therapeutic conjugates. Here, we develop streamlined assays that assess the binding kinetics of both the ASO and the targeting ligand using biolayer interferometry (BLI). The BLI biosensor facilitates immobilization of a biotinylated oligonucleotide, which can then hybridize an ASO conjugate and subsequently measure its binding affinity to the ligand target (e.g., antibody or receptor) through analysis of a BLI sensorgram. The utility of this biomolecular sandwich binding assay is demonstrated with phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomers (PMOs) and peptide nucleic acids (PNAs) conjugated to a peptide or protein ligand. We show that this assay can be used to detect cellular binding and predict in vitro efficacy. The methods developed here can be leveraged to accelerate the development of next-generation ASO therapeutics.

title: Developmental bias explains the evolutionary trend towards simple leaf shapes.
abstract: The relative influence of developmental bias and natural selection on evolutionary outcomes remains a central, unresolved question in evolutionary biology. Here, we combine large-scale phylogenetic trees with herbarium data to confirm that, across the evolutionary history of angiosperms, transitions from complex to simple leaf shapes have occurred at a significantly higher rate than the reverse. To investigate whether this directional trend reflects an underlying developmental bias, we simulate evolutionary transitions by introducing random mutations into a well-established computational model of leaf development. Despite excluding selection, the transition rates produced by the model closely align with those observed in the phylogenetic data. This agreement indicates that a strong developmental bias, reflecting the relative ease with which gene regulatory networks generate simple over complex leaves, has played a major role in shaping the evolution of leaf morphology. Our findings echo recent work showing that similar biases towards simplicity influence the evolution of molecular structures, including RNA secondary structures and protein quaternary assemblies. Together, these results suggest that a developmental bias favouring simplicity may be a widespread and general feature of evolutionary systems.
authors: Samuel H A von der Dunk

title: System-wide identification and regulatory network analysis of m⁶A-APA associated genes in Arabidopsis Thaliana.
abstract: N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A) modification and alternative polyadenylation (APA) are key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms that govern plant growth, development, and stress responses. Although emerging evidence suggests crosstalk between m⁶A and APA in plants, their system-level coordinated regulatory network remains poorly understood. Here, we established an integrated bioinformatics framework to systematically characterize the potential interplay between m⁶A and APA. This framework combines multi-sample correlation analysis of m⁶A modification levels and APA usages, along with random walk with restart (RWR) algorithm-based screening in protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks, to identify candidate genes with inferred m⁶A-APA association (called m6APAreg genes). We collected 56 methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (MeRIP-seq) datasets under diverse genetic backgrounds and stress conditions in Arabidopsis, and identified 2,505 m6APAreg genes using this integrated bioinformatics framework. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that these genes are significantly enriched in pathways related to metabolism, stress response, and developmental regulation. Orthogonal support from published datasets indicated a higher binding rate of the m⁶A reader CPSF30-L to m6APAreg genes, supported by stronger poly(A) signals. To further explore the potential regulatory hierarchy, we constructed multi-layered regulatory networks integrating m6APAreg genes, miRNAs, transcription factors, and poly(A) factors. Moreover, sample-specific analysis characterized condition-dependent correlation patterns, with the inferred regulatory direction and functional modules of the m⁶A-APA axis dynamically changing in response to genetic background and environmental stress. This study represents the first systematic attempt to prioritize candidate genes associated with the m⁶A-APA regulatory module in Arabidopsis. Our work provides novel insights into the potential complex interplay between epitranscriptomic regulation and 3' end processing in plants. The established analytical framework and the reservoir of candidate m6APAreg genes offer a valuable resource for future functional validation studies focused on plant development, stress responses, and crop improvement.

title: Molecular basis for DNA cleavage by the mini-RNA-guided endonuclease Casδ-1.
abstract: CRISPR-Cas adaptive immune systems are powerful and versatile tools for genome engineering. CRISPR-Casδ-1 is a recently discovered, evolutionarily distinct endonuclease that enables versatile cross-kingdom genome editing under miniature RNA-guiding. In this study, we present a comprehensive biochemical and structural characterization of CRISPR-Casδ-1. Biochemical analysis not only verifies that Casδ-1 exhibits robust double-stranded DNA cleavage activity and target-dependent trans-cleavage activity, but also explores in depth its precise cleavage sites and substrate saturation. Furthermore, we determine a 3.04 Å resolution cryo-EM structure of the Casδ-1-crRNA-dsDNA ternary complex, which reveals the molecular basis of protospacer-adjacent motif (PAM) recognition, crRNA-DNA heteroduplex assembly, and RuvC domain-mediated DNA cleavage. Collectively, our study reveals the structural basis and evolutionary insights into Casδ-1, advances the mechanistic understanding of type V CRISPR-Cas effectors, and offers opportunities for the rational design of CRISPR-Casδ-1 as a versatile genome-editing tool.

title: Reconstruction and Analysis of lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA ceRNA Network and Drug Repositioning to Identify Potential Biomarkers and Therapeutic Candidates for Colorectal Cancer.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent and life-threatening malignancies worldwide. Despite substantial advances in therapeutic strategies, CRC remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, largely due to late-stage diagnosis. Molecular-level investigation of disease mechanisms through bioinformatics approaches enables the identification of key biomarkers and regulatory pathways, facilitating early detection as well as the development of targeted and personalized therapies. CRC-specific differentially expressed miRNAs were identified using CRC-filtered datasets obtained from the dbDEMC database. Interactions among lncRNAs, miRNAs, and mRNAs were retrieved from the lncACTdb and miRTarBase databases. A competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network was constructed by integrating lncRNA-miRNA and miRNA-mRNA interaction networks. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was subsequently developed based on the identified target genes and analyzed using the MCODE algorithm to detect significant functional modules. Functional enrichment analysis was performed to explore the biological roles of the identified biomarkers. A drug-gene interaction network was constructed to identify potential therapeutic candidates. Finally, Pearson correlation analysis was performed to evaluate the co-expression relationship between lncRNAs and their corresponding mRNAs, and immunohistochemistry (IHC) data from the Human Protein Atlas (HPA) were utilized to validate differential gene expression. Network analysis led to the identification of twelve potential biomarkers associated with CRC, including five miRNAs (hsa-miR-142-5p, hsa-miR-424-5p, hsa-miR-98-5p, hsa-miR-139-5p, and hsa-miR-486-5p), four lncRNAs (NEAT1, XIST, LINC00665, and OIP5-AS1), and four protein-coding genes (PTEN, IGF1R, KRAS, and PIK3CA). Drug repositioning analysis identified Erlotinib, Metformin, and Gefitinib as potential therapeutic candidates for CRC treatment. This study presents a comprehensive bioinformatics framework for the identification of key biomarkers and potential therapeutic agents in CRC. Integration of lncRNA, miRNA, and mRNA interaction networks revealed critical regulatory elements and pathways involved in CRC progression. The proposed candidate biomarkers and drugs offer promising avenues for future research on colorectal cancer and may contribute to the development of targeted therapies and drug repurposing strategies.

title: SpatialMuSC: Spatial Graph-Conditioned Diffusion Refinement for Robust Spatial Multi-Omics Integration.
abstract: Emerging spatial multi-omics technologies enable the simultaneous profiling of multiple molecular layers within the same tissue section, offering new opportunities to interrogate tissue organization in its native spatial context. However, sequencing-derived spatial multi-omics data are often affected by intrinsic perturbations, such as technical noise, missing values, sparsity and measurement bias. These perturbations make existing methods that mainly use spatial graphs for neighborhood aggregation insufficient to recover continuous tissue-region structures, while unconstrained representation learning may propagate noisy associations and lead to fragmented spatial domains. We present SpatialMuSC, a robust spatial multi-omics integration framework centering on spatial graph-conditioned diffusion refinement and perturbation-invariant fusion consistency. SpatialMuSC introduces spatial topology as conditional information into the latent diffusion process, enabling spatial adjacency to guide neighborhood aggregation, spatial structure propagation and graph-aware denoising of latent states. Perturbation-invariant fusion consistency further encourages stable multi-omic fusion under perturbed observations. We evaluate SpatialMuSC on diverse spatial multi-omics datasets across different tissues and sequencing platforms, including 10x Visium, Stereo-CITE-seq, SPOTS and spatial epigenome-transcriptome data. Across these benchmarks, SpatialMuSC consistently outperforms ten state-of-the-art methods in spatial domain identification and tissue-structure preservation. Ablation analyses confirm the contributions of graph-conditioned diffusion refinement and perturbation-invariant fusion consistency, rather than post hoc graph smoothing or graph propagation alone. In particular, SpatialMuSC effectively distinguishes adjacent tissue regions, preserves block-wise smoothness and layered architectures, and shows more stable performance in missing-observation stress tests, while hippocampal marker, enrichment, and paired RNA-ATAC analyses identify a GCL-associated neuronal program and a TTR-associated accessibility feature in a choroid plexus-enriched domain. The source code is available at https://github.com/CSUBioGroup/SpatialMuSC. Supplementary data are available online.

title: Geometry and topology of DNA defects
abstract: DNA defects arise frequently, either as a result of damage, protein binding or the action of molecular enzymes such as an RNA polymerase. Here we combine geometry, atomistic simulations and an analysis of real DNA structures to provide a quantitative characterisation of DNA defects and their dynamics. The composite order parameter describing defects geometrically is a backbone-to-base polar vector, together with a quaternion capturing 3D base orientation in a single strand. There are three types of defects: flips of the polar vector, stacking defects of bases, and composite defects encompassing both. All types of defects feature in realistic structures for DNA and have functional relevance. Additionally, biased molecular dynamics simulations of DNA with an imposed elastic deformation form flip or stacking defects whose abundance and dynamics strongly depend on sequence and type of deformation. Our results provide a link between geometry and biochemistry, and could also be applied, for instance, to identify defects in RNA molecules and nucleosome arrays.

title: Read&Tag enables antibody-independent combinatorial and multifactorial chromatin profiling
abstract: Genome-wide chromatin profiling methods based on in situ tagmentation have expanded access to epigenomic information but generally rely on antibodies, thereby limiting their multifactorial capacity and the direct measurement of combinatorial chromatin states. Here, we introduce Read&Tag, in which engineered chromatin reader domains or intrabodies are fused directly to the Tn5 transposase to target specific chromatin features in situ. Read&Tag profiles active and repressive histone modifications, DNA methylation, and elongating RNA polymerase II, with signal amplitude increasing with target abundance and remaining robust in frozen tissue and low-input samples. Because the targeting module is a protein of defined structure and affinity, two specificities can be combined within a single complex. Tagmentation by such a dual-specificity reader requires H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 to be present together in the same chromatin fragment. The co-occurrence of both marks thus becomes a precondition of the measurement rather than an inference drawn from independently measured profiles. Combining barcoded reader-Tn5 complexes with primer-timed signal augmentation enables the measurement of four chromatin features in a single reaction. Read&Tag therefore provides a modular, antibody-independent platform for combinatorial and multifactorial profiling.

title: Quantifying (de)mixing of disordered proteins in molecular dynamics simulations.
abstract: Biomolecular condensates control the spatial and temporal organization of cellular biochemistry. Their architectures often arise from complex, multicomponent mixtures governed by weak, multivalent interactions between intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) of proteins. However, current approaches lack generalizable metrics to determine whether IDRs will mix or segregate within condensates. Here, we present a domain decomposition method (DDM) that accurately determines phase concentrations without identifying condensate interfaces. When tested against 399 IDR simulations, the DDM recovers dense- and dilute-phase concentrations within 1% agreement of established surface-based methods. By calculating spatial variances to map three-dimensional organization, this approach successfully distinguishes homogeneous mixing from surface enrichment, core-shell architectures, and complete segregation. Applying this continuous metric to 2,068 binary mixtures of 32 distinct IDRs, we demonstrate that physicochemical similarity strongly promotes mixing. Hydrophobic IDRs mixed promiscuously across all partner chemistries, whereas charged sequences mixed in a way highly sensitive to charge complementarity, forming the most stable condensates as net charge approached zero. Compared with experimental networks, our IDR-only simulations predicted the partitioning preferences for 10 of 13 proteins, with discrepancies accurately isolating cases where colocalization strictly requires RNA or folded domains. Quantifying mixing in this way provides a robust and reproducible method for predicting IDR interactomes and understanding the composition of complex cellular condensates.
extra: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

title: From Receptor to Reproduction: Molecular and Functional Characterization of NMDA Receptor Signaling in Bemisia tabaci Asia II-1.
abstract: N-methyl-d-aspartate receptors (NMDARs) are ionotropic glutamate receptors that regulate neuronal calcium signaling and intracellular secondary messenger pathways, playing pivotal roles in synaptic plasticity, neuronal development, and neurological disorders in vertebrates. Despite their evolutionary conservation, the molecular characteristics and physiological functions of NMDARs remain largely unexplored in insects. In the present study, we characterized and functionally validated two NMDAR subunits, Btab N1 and Btab N2, in the agricultural pest Bemisia tabaci using an integrated molecular, structural, pharmacological, genetic, and physiological approach. Spatial and temporal expression analyses revealed predominant expression in the head and thorax and elevated transcript abundance in pre-pupa and adults. Protein structural modeling predicted a conserved hetero-tetrameric receptor architecture, while molecular docking demonstrated favorable binding of the non-competitive antagonist MK-801 within the predicted channel pore. Pharmacological inhibition and RNA interference consistently suppressed NMDAR expression and disrupted downstream calcium signaling components, including calmodulin (CaM), calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII), cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB), protein kinase C (PKC), and nitric oxide synthase (NOS). This suppression was accompanied by significant downregulation of Juvenile Hormone Acid O-methyltransferase (JHAMT) and Vitellogenin genes, and a substantial ~32%-35% reduction of juvenile hormone titer in adults, pronounced as reduced oviposition, egg hatchability, and nymphal establishment in oviposition assay. Collectively, our findings establish NMDAR-mediated calcium signaling as a neuroendocrine regulator linking neuronal activity to juvenile hormone biosynthesis and reproductive fitness in B. tabaci, highlighting NMDARs as promising molecular targets for next-generation whitefly management.

title: Prophylactic and therapeutic antiviral effects of the influenza A defective interfering particle OP7 in human lung epithelial cells in vitro.
abstract: Defective interfering particles (DIPs) derived from the influenza A virus (IAV) are a promising antiviral agent due to their strong antiviral efficacy demonstrated in various animal models. OP7 is an unconventional IAV DIP with multiple point mutations in the viral RNA (vRNA) of genome segment 7, as opposed to the large internal genomic deletions typically found in conventional IAV DIPs. Furthermore, OP7 showed an even higher interfering efficacy than conventional DIPs. However, the inhibitory effect of OP7 on standard virus (STV) replication has primarily been investigated in Madin-Darby Canine Kidney cells, which lack a functional myxovirus resistance-mediated antiviral activity against IAV. In this study, we examined the antiviral activity and mechanism of antiviral action of an OP7 chimera, with a large internal deletion in segment 1 as well as point mutations in segment 7, in an IFN-competent human lung carcinoma cell line in vitro. We performed STV and OP7 co-infection experiments using a variety of infection conditions and measured the time-resolved dynamics in viral titre, vRNA, protein level and host cell gene expression. We observed that OP7 co-infection results in enhanced type I IFN responses and markedly reduced infectious virus release, even at low doses. Additionally, we found that at a high STV multipilicity of infection (MOI), the replication interference of OP7, suppressing the replication of STV vRNA, appears to be the dominant mechanism of its antiviral action. At a low MOI, however, IFN induction seems to be more important. Furthermore, we examined the efficacious co-infection time window for potential prophylactic and therapeutic antiviral treatment. We observed an antiviral effect exerted by OP7 infection for up to 7 days before STV infection and up to 24 h after STV infection. Together, these findings demonstrate that OP7 is a potent antiviral DIP. Therefore, this work supports the further development of OP7 as a therapeutic and prophylactic antiviral agent.

title: Broad-spectrum, small-molecule inhibition of coronavirus NSP10/14 exonuclease activity.
abstract: Over the past 30 years, highly pathogenic coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV, MERS, and SARS-CoV-2, have emerged and caused disease in the human population. Currently, antivirals are generally developed to be highly specific for a viral protein, making them susceptible to the development of resistant variants and limiting their breadth across viruses. Here, we report a strategy to identify small-molecule inhibitors targeting the relatively conserved coronavirus NSP14 exonuclease protein, prioritized for their breadth across divergent viral proteins. Using a FRET-based high-throughput screen of ~50,000 small-molecule compounds, followed by a series of orthogonal assays, we report the identification of a small-molecule inhibitor, ST095455, that targets the NSP10/14 complex. In addition to SARS-CoV-2, ST095455 inhibited the NSP10/14 complexs of five other CoVs, including endemic and seasonal strains. ST095455 displayed low-micromolar IC50 values in biochemical assays and inhibited SARS-CoV-2 replication in Vero E6 and A549-hACE2 cells, as well as primary epithelial ALI cultures, without obvious cytotoxicity. Dose-dependent reductions in viral RNA and infectious titers were observed, and viral RNA sequencing revealed a corresponding increase in viral genome mutations in progeny virus, consistent with impaired NSP14-proofreading activity. These findings demonstrate NSP10/14 complex as a conserved antiviral target and support future development of ST095455 as a pan-CoV antiviral therapeutic.IMPORTANCETo protect against future zoonotic coronavirus outbreaks, the development of broadly acting antivirals is a top priority. Most existing coronavirus therapeutics target SARS-CoV-2 enzymes and frequently display limited activity against genetically divergent coronaviruses. Here, we used a discovery pipeline that prioritized antiviral breadth from the earliest stages of screening and identified a small-molecule inhibitor of the highly conserved NSP10/14 proofreading complex with activity across multiple genetically distinct coronaviruses. Our lead compound suppressed viral replication and disrupted viral genome fidelity, supporting the concept of proofreading inhibition as a viable target of this virus family. These findings provide both a promising antiviral compound and a general strategy for developing countermeasures against future coronavirus-associated diseases.

title: Efficient Delivery of PIKFYVE mRNA-LNPs Rescues Lysosomal Dysfunction in PIKFYVE Knockout Lens Epithelial Cells.
abstract: PIKFYVE deficiency has been implicated in congenital cataract, and gene therapy based on PIKFYVE mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) represents a potential therapeutic strategy. We developed an SM-102-based LNP delivery system encapsulating human PIKFYVE mRNA with a long coding sequence, thereby overcoming the payload capacity limitations of conventional viral vectors. To evaluate this LNP system, we identified differentially expressed lysosomal genes via RNA sequencing and investigated its biocompatibility, transfection efficiency, and capacity to rescue lysosomal defects in PIKFYVE knockout lens epithelial cells (PIKFYVE-/-SRA01/04). Additionally, in vivo localized expression was assessed using firefly luciferase (FLuc) mRNA-LNPs administered via subconjunctival, intracameral, intravitreal, and subretinal injections in female C57BL/6J mice. The mRNA-LNP system exhibited high cytocompatibility and over 99% transfection efficiency in vitro. Treatment dose-dependently increased expression of PIKFYVE, partially rescuing lysosome-related transcripts and attenuating vacuolization in PIKFYVE-/-SRA01/04 cells. This functional restoration enabled the deficient cells to regain a nearly normal morphology, with the intracellular vacuolar area reduced from 14.29% to 7.98%. Furthermore, in vivo imaging demonstrated localized FLuc expression upon mRNA-LNP delivery across four ocular administration routes. This study demonstrates that the PIKFYVE mRNA SM-102-LNP delivery system effectively restores protein expression and rescues lysosomal dysfunction in PIKFYVE-/-SRA01/04 cells. LNP-mediated mRNA replacement represents a practicable, translatable strategy for PIKFYVE-associated cataracts. We constructed a PIKFYVE mRNA-LNP platform that restored protein expression, ameliorated lysosomal dysregulation, and significantly improved cellular morphology. These findings provide a proof-of-concept for an mRNA-LNP therapeutic approach to ophthalmic disorders.

title: Integrated m6A epitranscriptomic and metabolomic analysis reveals drought-responsive gene modules and regulators in wheat.
abstract: Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) is a major staple crop worldwide, yet drought stress severely limits its yield and quality. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) plays important roles in plant stress responses, yet its function in wheat drought adaptation remains largely unknown. Here, we integrated methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (MeRIP-seq) and widely targeted metabolomic analyses to characterize m6A modification dynamics in two wheat accessions with contrasting drought tolerance, L1773 (drought-tolerant) and L98 (drought-sensitive), under drought stress. L1773 exhibited drought-induced global m6A hypermethylation, whereas L98 showed no net change. Drought-responsive genes with differentially m6A-modified were enriched in photosynthesis, stress signaling, and protein homeostasis pathways underpinning the superior drought tolerance of L1773. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and two-way orthogonal partial least squares (O2PLS) identified a key co-expression module (MEbrown) associated with lignin biosynthesis. Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) assays revealed that two hub genes from this module, TaC3'H1 and TaERF160, negatively regulate drought tolerance, whereas TaNAC108 acts as a positively regulator. Furthermore, silencing the drought-responsive m6A reader gene TaECT3-2A significantly improved seedling survival rate, identifying it as a negative regulator of wheat drought tolerance. Collectively, this study delineates the m6A epitranscriptomic landscape of wheat under drought stress and identifies lignin biosynthesis as a key pathway targeted by m6A-mediated epitranscriptomic regulation, providing new insights into the epitranscriptomic contribution to crop drought adaptation.

title: Engineering Nitroimidazole-Based Molecular Elements for Hypoxia-Responsive Oligonucleotide Materials.
abstract: Hypoxia-responsive oligonucleotides (ONs) offer a route to conditionally regulate nucleic acid activity in diseased tissues, but the chemical factors that govern their masking and activation remain insufficiently defined. Here, we synthesized four nitroimidazole-modified phosphoramidite monomers derived from adenine (Ah), guanine (Gh), thymine (Th), and cytosine (Ch) and incorporated the Th, Ah, and Gh building blocks into ONs by automated solid-phase synthesis. Using a common parent sequence, we compared Th-, Ah-, and Gh-modified ONs in terms of synthetic compatibility, duplex stability, and reductive release, and further evaluated selected Th-modified ONs in cellular and in vivo studies. Thermal denaturation studies showed that internal Th and Gh modifications caused substantial destabilization of DNA/RNA duplexes, whereas Ah modifications were better tolerated. Under nitroreductase/NADPH reduction conditions, the Gh modification showed the most efficient regeneration of the native ON, while Ah mainly formed reduced but uncleaved products and Th gave partial release. Although Gh provided favorable masking and release behavior, Th offered a more practical balance of synthetic accessibility and duplex inhibition. Th-modified ONs retained Clusterin-silencing activity in MIA PaCa-2 cells and showed hypoxia-associated recovery of activity, and enhanced and prolonged tumor-associated fluorescence in tumor-bearing mice compared with an unmodified control. These results highlight the importance of the tested nucleobase-attachment-site combinations in the design of nitroimidazole-modified ONs.

title: Guide ssDNA Modulates the Recognition Selectivity of CRISPR-Cas12a for Direct miRNA Detection.
abstract: Owing to its robust trans-cleavage activity, CRISPR-Cas12a is a preferred tool for biosensing, yet its native DNA-only recognition limits RNA detection. Herein, we report a simple strategy requiring neither protein mutagenesis nor exogenous factors that enables wild-type Cas12a to directly detect RNA targets. We repurposed the Cas12a recognition unit from a full-length ssDNA into a cooperative assembly of two short ssDNAs. In this assembly, a 10-11 nucleotide primer segment relieves the inherent DNA restriction, enabling robust dual-DNA/RNA recognition. Notably, this primer ssDNA modulates substrate preference solely by remodeling the ribonucleoprotein complex conformation without directly triggering trans-cleavage, which remains strictly dependent on target-crRNA complementarity. Molecular docking simulations further reveal that the crRNA-target heteroduplex induces a conformational rearrangement in the Cas12a Nuc domain, forming a catalytic channel that supports trans-cleavage. Further, we constructed a primer ssDNA-mediated Cas12a platform that detects miR-122, miR-92a, and miR-192 with high specificity and sensitivity, rendering it suitable for early clinical diagnosis. Collectively, this work establishes a minimalist, low-cost strategy to overcome Cas12a's intrinsic RNA detection limitation, elucidates the underlying conformational mechanism, and provides a practical technological tool for rapid RNA diagnostics and integrated molecular diagnostic platforms.

title: Neutrophil-mediated delivery of paclitaxel and Bcl-2 siRNA reverses chemoresistance in bone-metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) bone metastasis remains a significant clinical challenge owing to limited drug across the blood - bone marrow barrier as well as the chemotherapy resistance. Overexpression of the anti-apoptosis protein B-cell lymphoma-2 (Bcl-2) and activation of ATP-binding cassette transporter-mediated drug efflux pathway contribute substantially to paclitaxel (PTX) resistance, leading to poor therapeutic outcomes. Herein, we developed a biomimetic bone-targeted nanotherapeutic by integrating neutrophil "hitchhiking" technology with hyaluronic acid (HA)-modified lipid nanoparticles co-loaded with PTX and Bcl-2 small interfering RNA (siRNA) (BP-HLNP@NEs) for the therapy of TNBC bone metastasis. Leveraging neutrophil-mediated bone marrow homing and HA-CD44 receptor-mediated active targeting, BP-HLNP@NEs efficiently traversed the blood-bone marrow barrier, enhanced accumulation within metastatic bone lesions, and reduced off-target toxicity in the liver and spleen. Following cellular internalization, the co-delivered PTX and Bcl-2 siRNA synergistically suppressed tumor growth by silencing Bcl-2 expression, inhibiting the NF-κB/P-glycoprotein resistance pathway, restoring chemosensitivity, and activating caspase-mediated apoptosis. In orthotopic bone metastatic TNBC models, BP-HLNP@NEs markedly inhibited tumor progression, reduced secondary lung metastasis, preserved bone architecture, and elicited antitumor immune responses. Collectively, this biomimetic delivery platform overcomes both biological delivery barriers and chemoresistance, providing a promising therapeutic strategy for the treatment of TNBC bone metastasis.

title: N/P ratio engineering enables safe and effective in vivo respiratory delivery of optimised LNP-siRNA antiviral therapy for SARS-CoV-2.
abstract: The development of safe and effective siRNA therapeutics for respiratory viruses, such as SARS-CoV-2, is hindered by poor in vivo stability and limited delivery to pulmonary tissues. The nitrogen-to-phosphate (N/P) ratio, which reflects the ratio between ionizable lipid amines (N) and siRNA phosphates (P), plays a critical role in siRNA encapsulation and delivery efficiency. Here, we investigate the impact of the nitrogen-to-phosphate (N/P) ratio on the performance of MC3 lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-siRNA formulations across N/P ratios of 3.2, 1.6, 1.2, and 0.8. LNP formulations at N/P 3.2 and 1.6 display superior encapsulation efficiency and intracellular delivery performance compared to lower ratios, with N/P 1.6 achieving antiviral efficacy comparable to N/P 3.2 in vitro, while showing reduced toxicity in vivo. In C57BL/6J mice, intranasal delivery of N/P 1.6 LNP-siRNAs induces neither detectable lung inflammation nor lung function impairment after single or repeated dosing, in contrast to N/P 3.2. In primary human bronchial epithelial cells cultured at the air-liquid interface (ALI-BECs), N/P 1.6 formulations reduce SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 replication in a dose-dependent manner, achieving > 5-log reductions in viral load. In a K18-hACE2 transgenic mouse model, intranasal administration of N/P 1.6 LNP-siRNAs significantly decreases lung viral RNA and infectious titres, while improving clinical scores. Collectively, these results demonstrate that tuning the N/P ratio to 1.6 optimises the balance between delivery efficiency and in vivo safety, providing a formulation design strategy for respiratory delivery of siRNA therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory pathogens.

title: Gene therapy for developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: a mechanism-driven framework for therapeutic design.
abstract: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are a group of severe neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by early-onset seizures, developmental delay or regression, and cognitive impairment. Many DEEs arise from genetic variants that disrupt neuronal excitability, synaptic function, metabolism, cell signaling, or epigenetic regulation. As the genetic architecture of DEEs has expanded, genetic therapy has emerged as a promising strategy to address their underlying molecular causes. Preclinical studies using adeno-associated viral vectors, antisense oligonucleotides, RNA-based therapies, and CRISPR-derived approaches have shown that early intervention can reduce seizure burden, improve neurological phenotypes, and extend survival in selected models. These advances also highlight the importance of therapeutic timing, cell-type specificity, and appropriate vector design. In this Review, we adopt a mechanism-centered framework that links major biological classes of DEEs to gene therapy design parameters, including modality, vector, promoter, and developmental timing, while also considering translational challenges and future directions for precision medicine in this field.

title: Helical repeat protein mRSiC is required for rRNA fragment accumulation in T. gondii mitochondria.
abstract: Myzozoans, including apicomplexan parasites Plasmodium falciparum and Toxoplasma gondii, possess unusual mitochondrial genomes that only encode two to three respiratory chain subunits and extensively fragmented rRNAs forming a divergent mitoribosome. Heptatricopeptide repeat (HPR) proteins are expanded in myzozoans, with some functioning as mitoribosomal constituents. Additional HPR proteins have been proposed to function in post-transcriptional mitochondrial gene expression, though their specific roles remain unexplored. We present a phylogenetic analysis of HPR proteins that reveals extensive lineage-specific expansions, consistent with diversifications of mitochondrial gene expression systems within myzozoans. We further characterize mRSiC, a HPR found in T. gondii and its closest relatives. Using sRNA sequencing and RNA gel blot analyses, we show that mRSiC is required for the stabilization of two lineage-specific mitochondrial sRNAs, RNA33 and RNA42. Loss of mRSiC causes rapid depletion of these RNAs, followed by secondary reductions of rRNA fragments, defects in the respiratory chain, and impaired parasite proliferation. Together, these findings highlight the importance of HPRs in apicomplexan mitochondrial gene expression and illustrate how lineage-specific RNA-binding factors support highly derived mitochondrial expression systems.

title: Photochemical internalization enhances in vivo immunity to peptide‑ and protein‑based vaccines with synthetic dsRNA adjuvants.
abstract: Efficient priming of antigen‑specific CD8⁺ T cells remains a major challenge for peptide‑ and protein‑based therapeutic vaccines targeting cancer and intracellular pathogens, despite the use of potent innate immune adjuvants such as synthetic double‑stranded RNA (dsRNA). In this study, we evaluated photochemical internalization (PCI), an endosomal escape technology, as a strategy to enhance vaccine‑induced immunity in combination with the dsRNA adjuvants poly(I:C) and poly‑ICLC. In mouse models, PCI combined with the SIINFEKL peptide and poly(I:C) increased circulating antigen‑specific CD8⁺ T cells by approximately 100‑fold compared with vaccination without PCI. Using a synthetic long HPV16 E7 peptide, PCI with poly(I:C) induced robust effector- and memory-phenotype CD8⁺ T‑cell responses and strong anti‑tumour activity in the TC‑1 HPV cancer model. PCI also enhanced CD8⁺ T‑cell priming induced by the clinically relevant telomerase vaccine UV1 when combined with poly‑ICLC. For larger protein antigens, including PPD, HBsAg, and KLH, PCI augmented CD4⁺ T‑cell responses and IgG production. Together, these findings establish PCI as a broadly applicable platform for enhancing peptide‑ and protein‑based vaccine immunity in combination with synthetic dsRNA adjuvants.

title: SEL1L knockdown impairs orthodontic tooth movement and periodontal bone remodeling.
abstract: Orthodontic tooth movement (OTM) depends on coordinated periodontal ligament (PDL) adaptation and alveolar bone remodeling. In this study, we investigated the role of suppressor of lin-12-like protein 1 (SEL1L) in these responses. An orthodontic force of 10 g was applied to the maxillary first molar of mice. Local Sel1l knockdown was achieved with an adeno-associated virus expressing Sel1l-targeting short hairpin RNA. Mouse and human PDL cells were subjected to cyclic tension. Osteogenic differentiation, yes-associated protein 1 localization, endoplasmic reticulum morphology, and intracellular calcium dynamics were examined. OTM and periodontal remodeling were evaluated by microcomputed tomography and histologic staining. Cyclic tension increased SEL1L expression in mouse and human PDL cells. Sel1l knockdown reduced osteogenic differentiation and yes-associated protein 1 nuclear localization and altered filamentous actin architecture, accompanied by endoplasmic reticulum dilation and altered calcium dynamics. In mice, local adeno-associated virus expressing Sel1l-targeting short hairpin RNA markedly reduced OTM, impaired tension-side bone microarchitecture and osteogenic activity, and decreased compression-side osteoclast activity. SEL1L supports PDL mechanoadaptation and coordinated bone remodeling during experimental OTM.

title: A dataset of RNA-seq and proteomic profiling of splenic CD4⁺ T cells in DSS-induced colitis mice treated with Akkermansia muciniphila.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease involves chronic inflammation of the intestine and disruption of normal immune balance, often linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis. The beneficial bacterium Akkermansia muciniphila (A.muciniphila) is known to support intestinal health and immune regulation, but its specific effects on T cell responses remain unclear. Here, we present a comprehensive multi-omics dataset integrating RNA sequencing and quantitative proteomics analyses of splenic CD4⁺ T cells derived from wild-type C57BL/6 J mice subjected to dextran sulfate sodium elicited colitis, in the presence or absence of A.muciniphila supplementation. The dataset includes transcriptomic profiles, protein abundance quantification, and quality control metrics for reproducibility. These data provide a valuable resource for exploring how A.muciniphila modulates immune metabolism, signaling, and inflammatory pathways in CD4⁺ T cells during intestinal inflammation, supporting future multi-omics integration and comparative analyses of host-microbe interactions in IBD models.

title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis.
abstract: Leukemia stem cells (LSCs) primarily rely on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) for energy production, a metabolic feature that inevitably generates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). NYNRIN (NYN domain and retroviral integrase containing) is highly expressed in LSC-like cells and is associated with poor prognosis in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Genetic targeting of NYNRIN impairs LSC-like cell maintenance and in vivo leukemogenic capacity in MLL-AF9- and HOXA9/MEIS1-driven AML models, and compromises the in vivo pathogenicity of patient-derived LSC-like cells. Mechanistically, NYNRIN sustains thioredoxin (Trx) activity by functioning as an RNA-binding protein that directly binds and degrades TXNIP mRNA via its NYN domain. Loss of NYNRIN stabilizes TXNIP mRNA, leading to TXNIP accumulation, which disrupts Trx-mediated redox buffering, induces ROS overproduction and mitochondrial dysfunction, and triggers LSC apoptosis. Notably, NYNRIN inhibition potentiates venetoclax efficacy by compromising Trx-mediated ROS clearance, lowering the apoptotic threshold of LSCs. Collectively, our findings reveal a critical NYNRIN-TXNIP-Trx axis that safeguards LSCs by enabling efficient ROS clearance.

title: LeCellModel: Interpretable Density Estimation over the Gene Expression Manifold
abstract: Representation learning for single-cell RNA-seq has been evaluated by the identities representations capture -- cell types, lineages, perturbations -- rather than how faithfully they model the distribution of cell states on the gene expression manifold. As a result, density estimation, rare-state detection, perturbation scoring, and gene-level attribution are bolted onto frozen embeddings as separate models, disconnected from the geometry of the data. We argue that modeling the distribution of cell states should be the primary objective, and that representation quality follows from it. Building on LeJEPA, whose SIGReg objective enforces a provably optimal isotropic Gaussian latent, we introduce LeCellModel, which reads the encoder's Jacobian log-volume (JEPA-SCORE) under this Gaussian latent as a relative typicality score. Across several datasets, LeCellModel outperforms established methods on the scIB benchmark for representation quality. Furthermore, we show that LeCellModel enables detection of rare expression states using JEPA-SCORE as a typicality measure, applying it to a controlled cytokine panel, where it identifies stimulated cells across minority fractions and tracks pathway-response magnitude. We introduce gene-level interpretability of the typicality score -- to our knowledge, the first method for analyzing JEPA-SCORE in feature space. Leveraging this framework, LeCellModel recapitulates the known association of a profibrotic macrophage program with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and discovers a CD177+ activated regulatory T cell subpopulation previously described only in tumor contexts. Both findings emerge directly from the geometry of the learned embedding, without relying on supervised annotations.

title: GBP1 Facilitates Th17 Differentiation via the NOD/NF-κB Signaling Pathway to Exacerbate the Inflammation of Intestinal Epithelial Cells.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a long-term inflammatory condition affecting the bowel. Understanding its causes and finding new treatment targets is crucial. Using proteomics, bioinformatics, and machine learning, we identified GBP1 and GBP5 as potential pathogenic molecules linked to UC. Furthermore, we evaluated the effects of GBP1 on inflammation in intestinal epithelial cells. Immunohistochemistry showed increased GBP1 and GBP5 expression in UC patients' intestinal tissues compared to healthy controls. The ROC curve demonstrated their diagnostic significance for UC. Western blot analysis revealed that GBP1 and GBP5 overexpression significantly elevated NOD1, NOD2, and p-RIP2 protein levels, with GBP1 showing a greater increase. Similarly, the NF-κB luciferase reporter assay indicated that GBP1 or GBP5 overexpression significantly boosted NF-κB transcriptional activity. ELISA results revealed that GBP1 or GBP5 overexpression significantly raised IL-6 levels, with GBP1 showing a greater increase. qRT-PCR showed that while GBP1 or GBP5 overexpression did not alter NOD1 and NOD2 RNA levels, it did elevate IL-6 RNA levels, especially with GBP1. Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed interactions between GBP1 and NOD1, and GBP5 and NOD2. Decreasing GBP1 levels reduced IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-17A cytokines, as well as NOD1, NOD2, phosphorylated RIP2, and phosphorylated NF-κB p65 proteins. Flow cytometry revealed that MC38 cells overexpressing GBP1 significantly raised CD4 + IL17A+ cell levels when co-cultured with mouse primary CD4+ naïve T cells. ELISA showed elevated IL-17A in the GBP1 overexpression group supernatant, and qRT-PCR indicated increased IL-17A and RORγt mRNA levels in T cells. These findings indicate that GBP1 overexpression may promote Th17 cell differentiation, activate the NOD/NF-κB pathway and aggravated UC, potentially providing a novel therapeutic target.

title: M-SCAN: Multi-Scale Constrained Analysis of Metabolic Networks for Genome-Scale Flux Inference in Pan-Cancer Cohorts.
abstract: Cancer metabolism reflects both recurrent tumour programmes and tissue-specific constraints, but transcriptome analyses do not directly estimate metabolic reaction fluxes. We developed Multi-Scale Constrained Analysis of Metabolic Networks (M-SCAN), a reproducible workflow for sample-wise genome-scale flux inference across heterogeneous cancer cohorts. M-SCAN retains the Human1 genome-scale metabolic network as a shared reaction backbone and introduces sample specificity through RNA expression, deleterious mutation effects, predicted kcat, direction-specific treatment of reversible reactions, and tissue-specific nutrient constraints. We benchmarked M-SCAN using measured exchange fluxes from 11 cancer cell lines and against an independent 13C-MFA dataset containing intracellular flux. Predicted and measured exchange fluxes were significantly correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.704, P < 0.001), and M-SCAN outperformed an enzyme constrained baseline in every cell line. We then applied M-SCAN to 7,562 tumour and normal samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas and the Genotype-Tissue Expression project across 14 cancer types. The flux profiles preserved tissue-specific metabolic structure, distinguished tumour from normal samples, and recovered flux programmes associated with clinical outcome and molecular subtype. Machine-learning analyses further identified recurrent tumour-associated pathways and stratified reactions into global-core, regional, and cancer-specific layers. M-SCAN provides a scalable and reproducible framework for integrating molecular, enzymatic, and environmental constraints into comparable sample-specific flux states. This framework complements RNA-based analyses by providing reaction-level flux representations for cohort-scale metabolic interpretation and hypothesis generation.

title: Case Report: Whole-exome sequencing revealing a novel PBX1 gene variant in a Chinese family with renal hypoplasia.
abstract: Congenital Anomalies of the Kidney and Urinary Tract with or without Hearing Loss, Abnormal Ears, or Developmental Delay (CAKUTHED) is an autosomal dominant syndromic form of congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract associated with heterozygous pathogenic variants in PBX1. The disorder is characterized by marked phenotypic variability. Identification of the underlying genetic variant can facilitate accurate prenatal diagnosis and genetic counselling of affected families. We recruited a Chinese family affected by CAKUTHED and performed chromosomal microarray analysis, whole-exome sequencing, and Sanger validation in available family members. Exploratory conservation, structural, and transcriptomic analyses were subsequently performed to investigate potential consequences associated with the identified variant. A novel heterozygous PBX1 variant, c.780C > A(p.Y260X), was identified by whole-exome sequencing and co-segregated with the renal phenotype among the available tested family members. The variant introduces a premature termination codon within the PBX1 homeodomain and is consistent with a predicted loss-of-function effect. Exploratory structural and transcriptomic analyses yielded hypothesis-generating observations but did not establish the molecular mechanism of the variant. We identified a novel heterozygous PBX1 variant, NM_002585.4: c.780C > A(p.Y260X), in a Chinese family with familial renal hypoplasia. The variant co-segregated with the renal phenotype among the available tested family members and is consistent with the established loss-of-function spectrum of PBX1-related CAKUTHED. The available evidence is most consistent with a haploinsufficiency mechanism; however, NMD of the mutant allele was not directly demonstrated, and a potential dominant-negative contribution from an NMD-escaped truncated protein cannot be formally excluded. The transcriptomic and molecular dynamics findings should be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating observations. Further allele-specific RNA analyses, NMD-inhibition experiments, direct protein detection, replicated simulations, and functional assays are required to distinguish between these potential mechanisms.

title: Accuracy of CRISPR/Cas-based nucleic acid detection for HIV-1: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: HIV continues to pose a substantial worldwide public health burden, and achieving the UNAIDS 95-95-95 goals depends on diagnostics that are reliable, rapid, and inexpensive. Because of its exceptional specificity and adaptable design, the CRISPR-Cas platform has emerged as an attractive option for nucleic acid detection. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we assessed the diagnostic accuracy of CRISPR-Cas-based assays for HIV-1, aiming to clarify their suitability for point-of-care testing and resource-limited settings. Web of Science, PubMed, and CNKI were searched through August 12, 2026. We included original studies that applied CRISPR-Cas assays to detect HIV-1 nucleic acids and reported sufficient data to construct 2 × 2 tables (TP, FP, FN, TN), with RT-qPCR for HIV-1 RNA or qPCR for HIV-1 DNA serving as the reference standard. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, and SROC curves were generated using a bivariate random-effects model. Subgroup analyses and meta-regression were performed to investigate heterogeneity. Nine studies met the inclusion criteria. The pooled sensitivity was 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98) and the pooled specificity was 0.98 (95% CI 0.93-1.00), with an AUC of 0.99. The I 2 statistic revealed low heterogeneity (11.82% for sensitivity and 8.91% for specificity). Publication bias was not statistically significant (Deeks' test, p = 0.925). When stratified by Cas protein, Cas12a yielded a sensitivity of 0.97 and a specificity of 0.98, while Cas13a showed a sensitivity of 0.93 and a specificity of 0.99. However, each subgroup comprised only four to five studies, and between-subgroup differences were not formally examined. The use of fluorescence readout did not significantly influence accuracy (p > 0.05). Studies using RPA/RAA amplification achieved accuracy comparable to the overall pooled estimates. In selected studies, CRISPR-Cas-based assays showed high sensitivity and specificity for HIV-1, but clinical equivalence to qPCR remains unproven. When combined with RPA/RAA isothermal amplification, it holds promise as a rapid, accurate point-of-care testing (POCT) tool. Nevertheless, limited studies and methodological concerns highlight the need for further multicenter validation and real-world implementation data. This systematic review and meta-analysis was registered with the Open Science Framework (OSF). The registration DOI is 10.17605/OSF.IO/AUTV8.

title: Integrative transcriptomic and network analyses reveal candidate genes associated with female sex determination in walnut (Juglans regia L.).
abstract: Walnut (Juglans regia L.) is monoecious, and its yield is constrained by the relatively few female flowers. Understanding floral sex determination may therefore help promote female flower formation. To investigate its molecular basis, we performed RNA sequencing on walnut flowers at representative developmental stages defined by morphological observation and paraffin sectioning. We identified 1284 sex-biased differentially expressed genes (DEGs) consistently differing between female and male flowers but not between stages within the same sex. Many DEGs were associated with morphogenesis and hormone-related pathways. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis refined this set to 554 female-associated candidate genes, with enrichment analysis highlighting the auxin signaling pathway. Protein-protein interaction analysis further identified 13 putative hub genes, including LOC108990244, an auxin response factor (ARF) family member. Most members of the ARF, auxin/indole-3-acetic acid (AUX/IAA), and transport inhibitor response 1 gene families members showed higher expression in female flowers, with several overlapping the candidate set. Quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction supported the expression patterns of selected candidates. Physiological measurements showed that the cytokinin-to-auxin ratio (cytokinin/IAA) declined during floral development but remained higher in female than male flowers. Collectively, these results identify candidate genes associated with female flower sex determination in walnut and suggest a potential role for auxin signaling.

title: A dynamically coordinated bioactive MOF-hydrogel system for ternary microenvironment reprogramming in MRSA-infected diabetic wounds.
abstract: Due to a persistent inflammatory response, excessive accumulation of ROS, and MRSA infection, the repair of diabetic chronic wounds faces severe challenges. Here, an intrinsically bioactive MOF-hydrogel system (SR@P/L) was designed to accelerate wound healing by reprogramming the multidimensional microenvironment. This system was based on poly (lipoic acid) and chitosan derivatives and was loaded with a novel strontium-rosmarinic acid MOF (SR-MOF). Dynamic disulfide, coordination, and hydrogen bonds formed a stable supramolecular network. Characterization revealed that the SR@P/L hydrogel displayed strong tissue adhesion, self-healing, and glucose-assisted stability. Moreover, it exhibited potent intrinsic antibacterial and antioxidant activities, as well as rapid hemostatic activity. Mechanistically, the SR@P/L hydrogel induced macrophage polarization from pro-inflammatory M1 to anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype through a ternary synergistic reprogramming effect of "immunomodulation, angiogenesis, and neurogenesis" and regulated the paracrine "cross talk" among multiple cell types. It also significantly enhanced the angiogenic capacity of vascular endothelial cells and the regenerative function of Schwann cells. In diabetic rats and large-animal models (mini-Bama pigs) with MRSA-infected wounds, the SR@P/L hydrogel promoted wound healing by accelerating granulation tissue formation and collagen remodeling. RNA-seq further revealed that the hydrogel promoted skin closure and functional recovery by coordinating adaptive immunity and tissue remodeling pathways. This multidimensional strategy presents a new design concept for treating refractory chronic wounds.

title: Interleukin 36γ-Mediated Barrier Disruption in Human Skin: Implications for Staphylococcus aureus-Induced Barrier Damage in Atopic Dermatitis.
abstract: Interleukin-36 (IL-36) plays a pivotal role in innate immunity and inflammatory responses, with its agonistic isoforms IL-36α/β/γ linked to the pathophysiology of atopic dermatitis (AD). Given that IL-36γ contributes to impaired keratinocyte differentiation in psoriasis and that IL-36α expression is regulated by barrier-disruptive S. aureus, we postulated a role for IL-36γ in skin barrier function and S. aureus-dependent barrier disruption in AD. To examine how IL-36γ affects human skin barrier function, we employed a 2D model of calcium-differentiated human keratinocytes (HNK) and a 3D model of ex vivo-in vitro air-liquid interface skin organ cultures. Gene and protein expression changes were measured by RT-qPCR and quantitative immunofluorescence microscopy, respectively, while barrier integrity was assessed through real-time cell analysis and transwell permeability assays. IL-36γ markedly reduced cell resistance and increased permeability in differentiated HNK, accompanied by decreased expression of differentiation markers and tight junction (TJ) proteins. Silencing IL1RL2 with specific siRNA restored IL-36γ-mediated skin barrier function and downregulation of filaggrin on RNA and protein levels. IL-36γ expression was upregulated by AD-associated S. aureus and viral mimics, including peptidoglycan, PSMα2, and Poly(I:C). Furthermore, IL-36γ stimulation of HNK resulted in an inflammatory response, implicating IL-1β, IL-6, and/or TNF-α as potential indirect mediators of IL-36γ-driven barrier disruption. Our findings indicate that the IL-36γ/IL1RL2 axis plays a significant role in skin barrier impairment in AD, suppressing differentiation markers and TJ proteins in both 2D and 3D skin models, while also pointing to its involvement in S. aureus-mediated barrier disruption.

title: Integrated Chromatin Accessibility and Transcriptomic Profiles Across Replicative Senescence Stages in Human Colonic Fibroblasts.
abstract: Cellular senescence is accompanied by widespread chromatin and transcriptional remodeling, but datasets that capture these changes across intermediate stages of replicative senescence remain limited. Here, we present an integrated bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq resource generated from primary human colonic fibroblasts spanning three replicative states: early-passage young cells, intermediate pre-senescent cells, and late-passage senescent cells. This serial design enables not only endpoint comparison between young and senescent cells but also stepwise evaluation of molecular changes during senescence progression. Bulk RNA-seq profiles captured transcriptome-wide alterations across the three states, while ATAC-seq defined corresponding changes in chromatin accessibility. By integrating promoter-associated accessibility with gene expression, we generated a gene-level multi-omic resource for evaluating concordant and discordant chromatin-transcription relationships across senescence transitions. The dataset also supports downstream analyses including pathway enrichment and transcription factor activity inference. Together, this dataset provides a useful resource for studying chromatin accessibility, transcriptional regulation, and their coupling during the progression of replicative senescence in human colonic fibroblasts.

title: ODC1-Mediated Polyamine Dysregulation Promotes Retinal Neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's Disease by Impairing Autophagy-Lysosomal Homeostasis.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) involves significant retinal pathology, but the underlying metabolic mechanisms remain unclear. Polyamine metabolism regulates neuronal and glial homeostasis, yet its role in the AD retina is unknown. We identified ornithine decarboxylase 1 (ODC1)-mediated polyamine dysregulation as a metabolic mechanism linking Müller glial dysfunction to impaired autophagy and retinal neurodegeneration in AD. Retinal polyamine levels and ODC1 expression were examined in AD retinas. ODC1 inhibition was achieved using α-difluoromethylornithine (DFMO) in vivo and small interfering RNA (siRNA) knockdown in human Müller glial cells. Retinal structure and function were assessed by histology, electroretinography, and visual behavior tests. Transcriptomic profiling, western blotting, and immunofluorescence evaluated autophagy-lysosomal homeostasis. Exogenous putrescine confirmed the metabolic specificity of ODC1-driven effects. The 5XFAD mouse retinas showed ODC1 upregulation, increased putrescine, reduced spermidine and spermine, and enhanced gliosis markers. Intravitreal Aβ1-42 induced sustained ODC1 expression, whereas DFMO suppressed inflammation, preserved retinal thickness, enhanced electroretinography, and improved visual behaviors. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses revealed that DFMO enhanced lysosomal- and autophagy-related transcriptional programs, with lysosomal-associated membrane protein 1 (LAMP1) restoration, p62 reduction, and LC3II/I normalization. In Müller cells, Odc1 knockdown attenuated Aβ-induced reactive changes, preserved lysosomal activity, and normalized autophagy signaling. Exogenous putrescine reversed these effects, confirming a functional link between ODC1-driven putrescine accumulation and autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction. Dysregulated polyamine metabolism drives retinal degeneration in AD. ODC1-mediated putrescine accumulation links Müller glial activation to impaired autophagy-lysosomal homeostasis, defective Aβ clearance, neuronal loss, and visual dysfunction. Targeting ODC1 with DFMO may represent a therapeutic strategy to preserve retinal structure and visual function in AD.

title: Neonatal hypoxia promotes pulmonary hypertension by upregulating ALKBH5 expression.
abstract: Postnatal hypoxia in high-altitude regions drives pulmonary developmental impairment in neonates, which may subsequently progress to pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular failure. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification regulates mRNA fate and cellular responses to stress; however, its role in neonatal PH remains unknown. In this study, we established a neonatal rat model of PH by chronic hypoxia exposure and investigated the role of the m6A demethylase AlkB homolog 5 (ALKBH5) using pharmacological inhibition, siRNA knockdown, and integrated m6A‑seq/RNA‑seq. Hypoxia reproduced the key features of pulmonary developmental impairment and pulmonary hypertension, including alveolar simplification, reduced vascular density, increased medial wall thickness, elevated right ventricular systolic pressure, and right ventricular hypertrophy. Hypoxia increased ALKBH5 protein in pulmonary vascular smooth muscle, which was inhibited by an ALKBH5 inhibitor 5-Carboxy-8-hydroxyquinoline. In pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), hypoxia increased ALKBH5 protein levels. ALKBH5 knockdown increased total m6A levels and suppressed proliferation and migration of PASMCs. Integrated MeRIP-seq/RNA-seq identified enolase 2 (ENO2) as a downstream target of ALKBH5 in PASMCs. ALKBH5 knockdown decreased ENO2 mRNA stability; ENO2 overexpression rescued proliferation and migration suppressed by ALKBH5 knockdown in PASMCs. Furthermore, hypoxia increased ALKBH5 promoter activity and expression via hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α), thereby promoting proliferation of PASMCs and pulmonary vascular remodeling. Targeting the HIF-1α/ALKBH5/ENO2 axis may represent a therapeutic strategy for neonatal PH.

title: Candidate role of ADAMTS2 in regulating keratinocyte apoptosis via indirect NF-κB modulation in life-threatening PD-1 inhibitor-induced TEN-like cutaneous toxicity.
abstract: Toxic epidermal necrolysis-like (TEN-like) immune-related cutaneous adverse event (ircAE) induced by programmed death 1 (PD-1) inhibitors is life-threatening; however, its pathogenesis remains unclear. This study aimed to dynamically characterize molecular signatures and identify potential pathogenic mediator(s) of TEN-like ircAE. Initial candidate mediators were identified through comparative analysis of bulk RNA sequencing data from distinct blood samples, coupled with a protein-protein interaction network. Subsequently, the potential pathogenic mediator(s), along with their primary cellular sources and corresponding effector events, were determined using quantitative PCR, tissue staining, single-cell RNA sequencing, and flow cytometry. Finally, validation was performed via in vitro cell experiments and in vivo rat models. By multiple comparisons among the sequencing data of progressive phase (Advanced stage), post-treatment recovery phase (Recovered stage), and matched controls (Control group) and following in vitro validation at the nucleic acid and protein levels, ADAMTS2 was identified as a promising candidate for further investigation. Subsequently, we showed that lesional fibroblasts were the primary cellular sources of ADAMTS2. Cultured human keratinocytes (HaCaT) were treated with supernatants from ADAMTS2-overexpressing fibroblasts (HDF-a), and the results showed that secreted ADAMTS2 promoted keratinocyte apoptosis via indirect inhibition of the NF-κB pathway. Furthermore, intradermal injection of an ADAMTS2-expressing plasmid in rats induced epidermal necrolysis-like lesions and keratinocyte apoptosis. Our study suggests that ADAMTS2 may serve as a candidate pathogenic mediator in PD-1 inhibitor-induced TEN-like ircAE. We have laid the groundwork for future studies on the pathogenesis and intervention targets of this life-threatening AE. These findings require validation with larger samples.

title: Polydatin Inhibits Pulmonary Vascular Remodeling in MCT-Induced PAH via STEAP4/PI3K/AKT Signaling.
abstract: Polydatin, a natural compound with recognized cardiovascular benefits, has shown preliminary protective effects against pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), though its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate its preventive potential and mechanisms as a complementary therapeutic candidate in a monocrotaline (MCT)-induced rat model of PAH. A rat PAH model was established using MCT. Polydatin was administered to evaluate its effects. Right ventricular structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and gross heart specimen analysis. Right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary vascular remodeling were assessed by histology and immunohistochemistry. Expression levels of α-SMA, PCNA, and ET-1 were measured. RNA sequencing was performed on lung tissues to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Key targets and pathways were further validated using qPCR and Western blot in both rat lung tissues and primary smooth muscle cells. STEAP4 function was confirmed by siRNA knockdown in primary arterial smooth muscle cells. Polydatin treatment significantly ameliorated PAH, improving right ventricular structure and function, reducing right ventricular hypertrophy (ANP/BNP), and inhibiting pulmonary vascular remodeling (α-SMA, PCNA, and perivascular collagen deposition). RNA sequencing identified DEGs modulated by polydatin, enriched in processes related to cell proliferation and differentiation. STEAP4 was identified as a key target reversed by polydatin at both mRNA and protein levels. Further validation confirmed that polydatin inhibits the activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway and suppresses cell proliferation. siRNA-mediated knockdown of STEAP4 reduced PI3K/AKT phosphorylation and inhibited ASMC proliferation, demonstrating that STEAP4 mediates the anti-proliferative effect of polydatin. Polydatin alleviates MCT-induced PAH and associated vascular remodeling primarily by downregulating STEAP4 and inhibiting the PI3K/AKT pathway. This highlights polydatin's potential as a preventive candidate for PAH.

title: Cross-species transcriptomic integration and experimental evaluation of THC-responsive signature genes identified by consensus machine learning.
abstract: Robust signature genes of Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) exposure remain difficult to identify because gene expression responses vary across species, tissues, and experimental conditions. Here, we developed an integrative framework combining cross-species transcriptomics, consensus machine learning, and targeted experimental evaluation to identify recurrent THC responsive molecular signatures. A total of 21 public RNA-seq datasets comprising 201 samples from humans, macaques, and mice were analyzed using a standardized pipeline incorporating ortholog mapping, ComBat batch correction, and leave-one-dataset-out cross-validation. Consensus feature selection using Elastic Net, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Stability Selection identified 22 high-confidence candidate signature genes. The ensemble classifier achieved an AUC of 0.719 and an average precision of 0.698. Functional enrichment analysis highlighted mitochondrial gene expression, mitochondrial translation, and endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein processing as major THC associated processes. RT-qPCR evaluation of eight representative candidates showed limited concordance for genes predicted to be downregulated. In contrast, upregulation-associated candidates showed substantially greater experimental concordance, with increased expression following THC treatment. Overall, these results provide partial and direction-dependent experimental support for the prioritized candidates, with greater concordance observed among upregulation-associated genes.

title: Single-molecule long-read sequencing reveals transcriptome complexity and enhances annotation in wild rice.
abstract: Wild rice species harbour extensive but largely uncharacterised transcriptional diversity that underpins key agronomic traits and represents a valuable resource for crop improvement. Here we integrate single-molecule long-read sequencing (Iso-Seq) with short-read RNA-seq to resolve transcriptomes of Australian Oryza rufipogon-like (O. rufipogon Aus) and O. meridionalis, the closest and most phylogenetically distant AA-genome relatives of Asian domesticated rice, respectively. Iso-Seq reveals substantially greater transcriptome complexity than represented in current reference annotations, identifying 48,876 transcript isoforms in O. rufipogon Aus and 69,180 in O. meridionalis. More than 60% of annotated genes are captured, and over 40% exhibit alternative isoforms, compared with approximately 10% in existing annotations. Integration of Iso-Seq data substantially improves genome annotations by restoring untranslated regions, increasing gene and transcript models, and improving BUSCO completeness. We identify 2,021 novel genes in O. rufipogon Aus and 2,645 in O. meridionalis, resolve hundreds of mis-assembled fusion genes, and uncover thousands of previously unannotated isoforms, including species-specific protein-coding transcripts and long non-coding RNAs. Analysis of three grain-size regulators (OsMADS1, GS1, and SGW5) reveals substantial isoform diversity in wild rice. Notably, functional OsMADS1 and GS1 isoforms previously identified in domesticated rice populations are also detected in wild species, demonstrating that multiple functional transcript variants exist prior to domestication. Iso-Seq further identifies O. rufipogon-specific splice variants and reduced SGW5 expression associated with its narrow-grain phenotype. Our findings uncover hidden transcriptional complexity in wild rice, substantially refine genome annotations, and provide valuable resources for functional transcript studies and precise isoform-level quantification.

title: Targeting zinc finger E-box binding homeobox 1 prevents osteoarthritic cartilage fibrosis and degeneration through epigenetically repressing the IL-17B/C/D pathway.
abstract: Accumulative evidence demonstrates that hyaline cartilage fibrosis and the resulting degradation of extracellular matrix are implicated in the pathology of osteoarthritis (OA). However, the mechanisms behind this remain largely undefined. Zinc finger E-box binding homeobox 1 (ZEB1) was identified as the most up-regulated transcription factor during OA progression using a regulon specificity score analysis on the public single-cell RNA sequencing dataset of human knee-joint tissues. The functional role of ZEB1 in OA and the underlying mechanism were evaluated using both conditional knockout mice combined with multiple OA models and primarily cultured OA chondrocytes. Tissue-specific in vivo gene editing of ZEB1 was applied to investigate the therapeutic effect of pharmacological targeting of ZEB1 in OA mouse models. ZEB1 is identified as an aberrantly activated transcription factor in the articular cartilage of human patients and mice with OA. Chondrocyte-specific and inducible deletion of ZEB1 in OA mice reduces hyaline cartilage fibrosis and degradation, osteophyte formation and joint inflammation, restraining OA progression. Mechanistically, loss of ZEB1 reduces histone acetylation on Il-17b/c/d and Il-17rb/rd promoters, thereby epigenetically repressing IL-17B/C/D signalling, a critical pathway that supports OA progression through up-regulating pro-fibrogenic and pro-inflammatory pathways. Treatment with recombinant IL-17D protein fully restores the impaired OA progression in ZEB1-deleted mice. The microneedle-lipid nanoparticle-mediated co-delivery of Cas9 mRNA and single-guide RNA achieves knee joint-specific in vivo gene editing of ZEB1, providing an effective protection against OA in mice. ZEB1 may serve as a promising therapeutic target for OA.

title: Aging impairs CX3CL1 neuroprotection in α-synuclein-induced Parkinson's disease pathology.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most prevalent movement disorder, is pathologically defined by the accumulation of α-synuclein (α-syn), loss of dopaminergic neuron and inflammation in the substantia nigra pars compacta. The neuronally expressed chemokine CX3CL1 (fractalkine, FKN), when delivered as the soluble form (sFKN) via AAV-mediated overexpression, protects dopamine neurons in several animal models of PD. Since aging is a major risk factor for PD, we examined the effects of sFKN overexpression in both young and aged PD models. To model PD, young (3-month) and aged (15-month) male F344 rats received unilateral intracranial injections of recombinant adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (rAAV9) encoding either human wild-type α-synuclein (α-syn) or green fluorescent protein (GFP). Motor performance was evaluated at baseline, 1 month, and 2 months post-injection. Behavioral deficits and neuropathological changes were compared across treatment and age groups. CX3CL1 involvement in PD-related neuroinflammation was assessed using immunohistochemistry and biochemical analyses and bulk RNA-seq was used to characterize transcriptomic changes. We found that sFKN rescued both motor deficits and dopaminergic neuron loss in young PD animals but not in aged animals. Analysis of the transcriptomics revealed age-dependent alterations in inflammatory, immune, and neurogenic signaling in response to sFKN treatment. In conclusion, while sFKN effectively ameliorates behavioral deficits and dopaminergic neurodegeneration in young PD animals, its protective effects are lost in aged animals. These findings emphasize the necessity of rigorous age-inclusive preclinical evaluation and suggest that targeting CX3CL1 signaling alone may be insufficient as a therapeutic strategy in age-related neurodegenerative disease.

title: Layer-Weighted Source-Anchored Transfer Learning for Multi-Omics Survival Prediction and Risk Stratification in Younger Breast Cancer Patients
abstract: Background- Younger breast cancer patients (<50 years) often present with more aggressive disease and distinct molecular characteristics, yet predictive models for this group are underpowered due to small sample sizes. Most existing models are built on older populations and may not translate directly, particularly across multiple omics data types. To address this, we developed Layered Source-Anchored Transfer Elastic Net (LSAT-EN), which adaptively borrows from the older source cohort while allowing borrowing strength to vary across omics layers according to their similarity between source and target cohorts, while performing EN variable selection. Methods -Patients aged [≥]60, [≥]55, and [≥]50 years were used as the source to improve prediction in patients aged <50 years. LSAT-EN were evaluated in group-correlated simulations and in TCGA-BRCA integrating 6 omics layers. Binary survival at 2-4 years was assessed by AUC; censored survival by Harrell's C-index and 2-5-year inverse probability of censoring weighted (IPCW) AUC. Results - In simulation, LSAT-EN achieved the highest AUC under moderate source-target heterogeneity ({sigma}=0.25; 0.747-0.802), outperforming GAS-EN (0.735-0.767), overall EN (0.683-0.710), individual EN (0.646-0.767), and glmtrans EN (0.640-0.733) across target training sample sizes (nT). Its advantage was greatest under higher source-target heterogeneity ({sigma}=4), particularly with small nT, where LSAT-EN achieved AUCs of 0.689-0.789 compared with 0.590-0.771 across competing methods. In TCGA-BRCA data, LSAT-EN improved discrimination relative to overall and individual EN in all binary and Cox models across all time horizons and source age groups.
