LSAT-EN was robust in stratifying high and low risk groups across molecular and clinical subgroups, while LSATEN-derived risk scores captured breast cancer-relevant pathway in survival models across time horizons, along with identifying most important miRNA signals. Conclusion- LSAT-EN is a powerful TL method for improving prediction and risk stratification for younger breast cancer patients; The framework may support prediction in other underrepresented populations with limited target-cohort data to advance cancer disparity ML research.

title: Icariin targets Rho family GEF FARP2 to modulate GTPase signaling for neuroprotection.
abstract: Oxidative stress is a primary driver of neuronal injury in neurodegenerative conditions including ischemia stroke (IS). Icariin (ICA), a natural flavonoid, exhibits neuroprotective activity. However, its direct molecular target remains elusive. Here, we identified the direct protein target of ICA and elucidated the downstream pathways mediating its protection against hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-induced neuronal injury. Neuronal B35 cells were treated with H2O2 to induce oxidative stress. Cell viability was evaluated using CCK-8 assays and Calcein-AM/PI double staining. The direct binding target of ICA was screened by drug affinity responsive target stability-mass spectrometry (DARTS-MS) proteomics, followed by validation through molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations as well as cellular thermal shift assay coupled with Western blot (CETSA-WB). RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) was performed to identify involved the signaling pathways. Network pharmacology and machine learning approaches including LASSO, random forest, and support vector machine, were applied to identify hub genes associated with IS. Finally, WB, phalloidin staining and siRNA-mediated FARP2 knockdown rescue experiments were performed to confirm the effects and mechanism of icariin in IS. ICA dose-dependently restored B35 cell viability following H2O2 exposure. FARP2 was identified as a direct binding target of ICA. Molecular docking and MD stimulations validated stable ICA-FARP2 binding (ΔG_bind = -21.38 ± 2.19 kcal/mol) driven by van der Waals and electrostatic interactions with Thr914 and Gln907. Transcriptomic profiling indicated that H2O2 exposure upregulated RhoGTPase signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and cilium assembly pathways. Integrated analyses further identified caspase-3 as a core regulatory gene and implicated Rap1 and PI3K-Akt signaling in IS. Finally, the functional validation confirms that FARP2 siRNA blocks the protective effect of icariin against H2O2-induced B35 cell injury. Conclusion: ICA exerts neuroprotective effects against H2O2-induced neuronal injury by targeting FARP2 and modulating RhoGTPase and PI3K-Akt signaling, suggesting its potential in regulating cytoskeletal dynamics and cellular stress responses.

title: An SPP1-Associated Macrophage State Marks Lesion-Centred Inflammatory Persistence During Subacute Spinal Cord Injury.
abstract: Persistent subacute neuroinflammation limits tissue repair after spinal cord injury (SCI), yet how macrophage state heterogeneity is organized within lesion-centered inflammatory niches remains unclear. We integrated time-resolved mouse single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics with trajectory analysis, regulatory network inference, ligand activity analysis, exploratory in silico Spp1 perturbation, and interpretable machine learning, followed by tissue-level and donor-recipient validation. Time-resolved profiling revealed early neutrophil and monocyte recruitment, subsequent macrophage accumulation, and delayed microglial activation. Macrophage subclustering resolved seven injury-responsive states comprising inflammatory, transitional, tissue-associated, lipid-associated, SPP1-associated, repair-associated, and homeostatic programs. Among these states, SPP1_Mac expanded prominently, peaked at 7 days post-injury, and retained marked inflammatory activity. Spatial mapping localized the SPP1_Mac signature and focal Spp1 expression to lesion-centered regions within a broader Cd44-enriched cellular territory. Regulatory network, ligand activity, communication, and machine learning analyses prioritized SPP1-associated signaling within this state-niche organization. Injured spinal cords showed increased lesion-associated SPP1 and CD44 expression and enrichment of SPP1 within IBA1-positive myeloid regions. In a BV2-to-RAW264.7 donor-recipient system, donor cell Spp1 silencing attenuated recipient cell CD44 and CD86 expression, the proportion of F4/80⁺CD86⁺ cells, and IL-1β and TNF-α secretion following conditioned medium transfer. Together, these findings support a state-niche-communication framework in which SPP1_Mac represents a prominent cellular feature associated with lesion-centered inflammatory persistence during subacute SCI, providing a biological foundation for further stage-informed investigation of the post-SCI inflammatory microenvironment.

title: Hypoxia drives ERO1A-dependent angiogenesis in ovarian cancer cells promotes peritoneal metastasis and platinum resistance.
abstract: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is characterized by early peritoneal dissemination and frequent platinum resistance, yet the epithelial states and mechanisms that couple metastasis, angiogenesis, and therapy response remain incompletely defined. We integrated in-house single-cell RNA sequencing of 82,149 cells from 21 treatment-naïve HGSOC specimens with external spatial transcriptomic and single-cell datasets to identify metastasis-associated epithelial programs. A hypoxia-enriched epithelial subcluster (E04) was preferentially expanded in advanced and metastatic lesions, showed high copy-number burden, and was defined by strong ERO1A expression. Spatial analyses and multiplex immunofluorescence showed that ERO1A-positive tumor cells were preferentially associated with endothelial niches and VEGFA-rich regions. Mechanistically, hypoxia induced ERO1A in a HIF1α-dependent manner, whereas ERO1A promoted VEGFA secretion mainly by facilitating disulfide bond-related oxidative maturation rather than by markedly increasing VEGFA transcription or total protein abundance. Functionally, ERO1A enhanced migration, invasion, angiogenesis, and cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer cells. Clinically, high ERO1A expression was associated with shorter platinum-free interval. In orthotopic models, intraperitoneal cisplatin plus the ERO1A inhibitor EN460 produced stronger antitumor effects than either monotherapy, and VEGFA knockdown largely abrogated this additional in vivo benefit, indicating that VEGFA-dependent angiogenesis is required for the full efficacy of the combination. These findings identify a conserved hypoxia-HIF1α-ERO1A-VEGFA axis that links pro-angiogenic secretion to peritoneal metastasis and platinum resistance, and support ERO1A inhibition plus platinum as a rational therapeutic strategy in advanced HGSOC.

title: GATA2-mediated IER3 transcription promotes breast cancer progression and tumor-associated immunosuppression.
abstract: The molecular mechanisms linking breast cancer (BC) progression to an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment remain incompletely understood. We investigated the role of the GATA2/IER3 axis in BC progression and immune-related cellular responses. Bulk transcriptomic datasets GSE10810 and GSE42568 and the single-cell RNA sequencing dataset GSE161529 were integrated with immune-related gene lists. Support vector machine-recursive feature elimination, The Cancer Genome Atlas data, and immune-infiltration analyses prioritized candidate genes. Expression was evaluated in BC tissues and cell lines. Knockdown and rescue experiments assessed BC cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and invasion, together with CD8+ T-cell responses and macrophage markers in coculture. Chromatin immunoprecipitation-qPCR and dual-luciferase reporter assays examined transcriptional regulation, and nude mouse xenografts assessed tumor growth. Immediate early response 3 (IER3) was upregulated in BC tissues and cells and was associated with an immunosuppressive infiltration profile. IER3 knockdown inhibited BC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion and increased apoptosis. It also enhanced CD8+ T-cell proliferation and interferon-γ secretion, reduced T-cell apoptosis, and decreased the proportion of CD206-positive macrophages. GATA binding protein 2 (GATA2) bound to the IER3 promoter and activated transcription. IER3 overexpression partially reversed the effects of GATA2 knockdown on BC cells and cocultured immune cells. In vivo, GATA2 knockdown reduced tumor growth, increased CD86 staining, and decreased CD206 staining; IER3 overexpression partially attenuated these effects (all p < 0.05). These findings support a role for GATA2-mediated IER3 transcription in BC progression and immune-related cellular responses. Its effects on adaptive antitumor immunity in vivo require further investigation.

title: Fibroblast growth factor 21 mediates pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease via the NRF2/GPX4 axis.
abstract: Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent metabolic disorder among pediatric populations. Fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) is a key regulator of hepatic metabolism; however, the mechanisms underlying its contribution to the pathogenesis of pediatric MASLD remain unclear. The aim of this study was to assess the role of FGF21 in obesity-associated MASLD and to examine the involvement of ferroptosis in this pathological process. In a cross-sectional cohort, serum concentrations of FGF21, 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE), and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in children with obesity and biopsy-confirmed MASLD. Subsequently, a murine model of MASLD was established by high-fat diet feeding, followed by assessment of body weight, blood lipid profiles, and serum FGF21 concentrations. Hepatic lipid accumulation and histopathological changes were assessed using hematoxylin and eosin staining, Oil Red O staining, and Masson staining. Serum ferroptosis-related biomarkers, including 4-HNE, glutathione (GSH), and the GSH/ oxidized glutathione (GSSG) ratio, were quantified by ELISA, whereas hepatic ferroptotic changes were examined by transmission electron microscopy. Quantitative polymerase chain reaction demonstrated reduced messenger RNA (mRNA) expression of FGF21, NFE2L2, and GPX4, whereas immunoblotting confirmed decreased protein expression of FGF21, NRF2, and GPX4 in samples from both children with MASLD and mice with high-fat diet-induced obesity. To investigate the functional role of FGF21, lentiviral-mediated knockdown of FGF21 was performed in HepG2 cells. Silencing FGF21 restored NRF2-GPX4 signaling and markedly attenuated hepatocellular lipid accumulation, indicating that suppression of this antioxidant pathway contributes to hepatic steatosis. Collectively, these findings suggest that FGF21-mediated ferroptosis may represent a mechanistic link between obesity and pediatric MASLD and identify the FGF21/NRF2/GPX4 axis as a potential therapeutic target.

title: DiffKnock: diffusion-based knockoff inference for neural networks with applications to single-cell RNA-sequencing data.
abstract: High-throughput single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) technologies have revolutionized our ability to characterize cellular heterogeneity and dissect gene regulatory mechanisms. These data, however, are inherently high-dimensional and correlated, posing substantial challenges for statistical inference and feature selection. Identifying disease-related genes, while rigorously controlling false discoveries, remains a key challenge in scRNA-seq data analysis. Traditional methods often rely on parametric assumptions, which may fail to capture complex relationships and can suffer from inflated false discovery rates (FDRs) in high-dimensional settings. We introduce DiffKnock, a diffusion-based knockoff framework for high-dimensional feature selection with finite-sample FDR control. DiffKnock addresses two key limitations of existing knockoff methods: preserving complex feature dependencies and detecting nonlinear associations. Our approach leverages diffusion models to generate valid knockoffs and employs neural network-based gradient and filter statistics to construct antisymmetric feature importance measures. Through simulations, DiffKnock demonstrates higher power than autoencoder-based, GAN-based, and Gaussian-based knockoff methods while maintaining target FDR, indicating superior performance in scenarios with complex nonlinear relationships. By applying the method to murine single-cell RNA-seq data of LPS-stimulated macrophages, we also identified canonical NF-$\kappa $B target genes (Ccl3, Hmox1). In another application to Religious Orders Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project donor-level pseudobulk transcriptomic data, DiffKnock further identifies a strong microglial signal for CERAD score, with PTPRG emerging as the most stable selected gene under both gradient- and filter-based statistics. These results highlight that, by combining flexible deep generative models with rigorous statistics, DiffKnock is a powerful and reliable tool for analyzing scRNA-seq data and other high-dimensional structured data.

title: Cross-regional and transcript-level prioritization of alternative-splicing events in autism cortex.
abstract: Selecting splice events for functional studies requires disease-associated RNA measurements to be connected to regulatory context and explicit transcript consequences. We developed an event-level prioritization framework for this task in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We integrated 34,025 published cortical splicing tests with regional direction, donor-aware sensitivity analyses, external cortical datasets, neural RNA-binding-protein data, and reconstructed coding branches. An effect-size-informed rule identified 278 exploratory candidates; no cortical event met transcriptome-wide false-discovery-rate (FDR) significance (minimum FDR = 0.1969). Among direction-evaluable events, 183/267 candidates were concordant in cerebellum, compared with 14,405/26,915 background events (68.5% versus 53.5%; odds ratio [OR] = 1.89). Because 46/48 cerebellar donors also contributed cortex, this comparison measures same-cohort coherence, not independent replication. RBFOX2 overlap showed a model-dependent adjusted association (OR = 1.94), without significant within-gene or binding-permutation support. Separate healthy motor-neuron datasets showed adjusted ORs of 2.16 and 2.13 (both q = 0.0059). Coding reconstruction classified 92/148 coding-overlap events as in-frame changes and distinguished transcript-dependent consequences; a PKM exon exchange preserved protein length while substituting 22 amino acids. External ASD analyses did not establish FDR-corrected replication, and baseline-adjusted neural SRRM4 comparisons were nonsignificant. The framework nominated 18 events under the complete-coding-model scope, including 13 retained under the stricter scope; both branches were observed for 12/18 and 11/18 in separate fetal bulk and single-cell catalogs. The resulting resource connects each nomination to a defined regulatory or coding rationale and an identifiable transcript structure, providing a focused basis for isoform-resolved experimental studies.

title: Recurrent cholesterol-enriched cartilage signature and SREBF1-sensitive lipid and catabolic responses in osteoarthritis.
abstract: The aim in this study was to identify a sterol-associated transcriptional program recurrent across human osteoarthritis (OA) cartilage datasets and test whether SREBF1 influences lipid metabolism and catabolic responses in chondrocytes. We used GSE220243 for donor-level, state-resolved discovery, GSE169454 for independent donor-level testing, and GSE114007 for platform-adjusted analysis of whole-cartilage RNA-seq profiles. We prioritized the cholesterol-homeostasis-associated module PM214 on biological grounds and evaluated its 27-gene signature across cohorts. SREBF1 activity inference was accompanied by a sensitivity analysis excluding shared regulon genes. Two independent SREBF1 siRNAs were tested in C28/I2 cells by RT-qPCR (six independent experiments) and immunoblotting (four experiments). Further experiments measured cellular cholesterol, triglycerides, MMP13 secretion, and the effects of genetic re-expression under interleukin-1β (IL-1β) stimulation (six independent batches per module). The Hallmark cholesterol-homeostasis component of PM214 was enriched in hypertrophic/ossifying chondrocytes (NES 2.124; FDR 3.74 × 10-4; 19 leading-edge genes). The 27-gene PM214 score was higher in OA-associated profiles in GSE169454 (exact P = 0.0286) and GSE114007 (platform-adjusted P = 8.00 × 10-4). Although SREBF1 was prioritized by transcription-factor activity analysis, its correlation with PM214 declined from 0.797 to 0.224 after eight shared genes were excluded (matched-null P = 0.582). Both siRNAs reduced four prespecified sterol-related transcripts, mature SREBP1 and HMGCR protein, cellular total cholesterol and triglycerides, and IL-1β-stimulated MMP13 secretion. Re-expression of siRNA-resistant SREBF1 restored key cholesterol, triglyceride, and MMP13 responses. PM214 is a recurrent OA-associated cartilage expression signature with a prominent cholesterol-homeostasis component. SREBF1 perturbation and rescue implicate this factor in lipid and catabolic responses in C28/I2 cells, without establishing direct regulation of the complete PM214 program or effects in primary human cartilage.

title: Oncogenic Ppm1d mutations deregulate the p53 pathway in primary mouse gliomas.
abstract: High-grade gliomas such as diffuse midline glioma (DMG) are incurable brain tumors with limited treatment options. A subset of high-grade gliomas harbor somatic, truncating mutations in exon 6 of phosphatase PPM1D, which stabilize the protein and deregulate p53 signaling. However, the consequences of these mutations for tumor initiation, progression, and therapy remain unclear. We developed a conditional Ppm1d-loxP-exon6-loxP-exon6-E518X-tag mouse allele (Ppm1d-flex-6) that enables lineage-, spatial-, and temporal-specific expression of a glioma-derived truncated Ppm1d protein from its endogenous locus in the presence of Cre-recombinase. Ubiquitous activation of mutant Ppm1d was modeled using the Meox2-Cre driver, and primary gliomas were modeled using the RCAS/tv-a system to introduce Cre and PDGFB co-drivers into Nestin-positive neural stem cells. Complementary studies were performed in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) expressing truncated Ppm1d following Cre recombination. While Meox2-Cre-driven ubiquitous recombination of Ppm1d-flex-6 produced muted phenotypes, Ppm1d-flex-6 recombination in Nestin+ neural stem cells accelerated gliomagenesis. Its oncogenic effect was weaker than complete p53 loss, and it did not accelerate tumorigenesis further in p53-null tumors. Single-cell RNA-sequencing revealed that Ppm1d-flex-6 gliomas adopt more progenitor-like transcriptional states and upregulate p53- and cell cycle-associated pathways. In MEFs, Ppm1d-flex-6 enhanced proliferation and shifted transcriptomic programs toward MAPK and PI3K-Akt signaling, while impairing DNA damage responses, including reduced γ-H2AX induction after irradiation. These defects sensitized cells to radiation and decreased clonogenic survival after ionizing radiation and PARP inhibition. Ppm1d mutations confer intermediate suppression of the p53 pathway, consistent with the clinical features of PPM1D-mutant gliomas and are associated with radiosensitivity and PARP inhibitor vulnerability.

title: Associations Between Monocyte Activation and Collagen Turnover Biomarkers With Subsequent Clinical Events in People With HIV-A Nested Case-Control Study Among Participants in the INSIGHT ESPRIT, FIRST, SMART, and START Trials.
abstract: While monocyte activation has been linked to cardiovascular disease (CVD) in people with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), its relationship with non-CVD comorbid conditions remains unclear. Similarly, the relationship between collagen turnover markers and HIV-related comorbid conditions has been understudied. We conducted a case-control study among participants in the Evaluation of Subcutaneous Proleukin in a Randomized International Trial (ESPRIT), Flexible Initial Retrovirus Suppressive Therapies (FIRST), Strategies for Management of Antiretroviral Therapy (SMART), and Strategic Timing of Antiretroviral Treatment (START) trials. Case patients were participants who experienced a composite outcome of AIDS/AIDS-related death (AIDS) or serious non-AIDS (SNA) event/non-AIDS-related death. Two matched controls were identified within trial by treatment group, age, and randomization date. Separate conditional logistic regression models (unadjusted and adjusted) estimated odds ratios for associations between baseline monocyte activation and collagen turnover markers with the composite and component outcomes. The cohort included 1487 participants, 498 case patients and 989 controls. Their median age was 44 years, and their median CD4 cell count was 539/µL; 19% were Black. Case patients included 189 with AIDS, 324 with SNA events, 159 with death from any cause, 168 with cancer, and 131 with CVD. Higher levels of monocyte activation markers (soluble CD14, soluble CD163, and monocyte chemoattractant protein 1) were associated with higher odds of the composite outcome (unadjusted odds ratios per 2-fold higher biomarker [95% confidence interval], 1.75 [1.37-2.24], 1.55 [1.31-.85], and 1.67 [1.35-2.07], respectively), largely driven by SNA events. Associations remained significant after adjustments for sex, race, and baseline CD4 cell count and HIV RNA, D-dimer, interleukin 6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels. Levels of collagen turnover markers tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases 1 and N-terminal propeptide of type III procollagen were associated with the composite outcome, but these associations were no longer significant after adjustment for D-dimer, interleukin 6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein. In HIV-related comorbid conditions, monocyte activation may play a role independent of systemic inflammation, and collagen deposition may reflect microscopic tissue injury associated with end-organ damage.

title: Abundance of carboxylesterase 1 in liver tissue and plasma-derived extracellular vesicles: Considerations for model-informed precision dosing.
abstract: Precision dosing requires accounting for variability in drug elimination capacity. Liquid biopsy, based on cell-free RNA (cfRNA) from plasma-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), offers a minimally invasive approach to characterize hepatic enzymes. The present study extends this framework to carboxylesterase 1 (CES1), an important determinant of exposure to prodrugs and active drugs. Matched liver tissue and plasma from 29 liver cancer patients were processed to measure CES1 protein (tissue proteomics) and cfRNA (RNA-seq of plasma-derived EVs). Individualized physiologically based pharmacokinetic models were generated to test the feasibility of model-informed precision dosing of D-methylphenidate and oseltamivir. CES1 cfRNA in plasma EVs (0.79 ± 0.62 reads per million [RPM]) was correlated with protein abundance in liver (942.98 ± 427.04 pmol/mg protein) from the colorectal liver metastasis cohort (Pearson's r = .57, p = .003, n = 25). Individual cfRNA measurements were projected into hepatic CES1 abundance-based dosing inputs for simulations. Sensitivity analyses revealed that the determinants of exposure variability were CES1 abundance for D-methylphenidate and renal function for oseltamivir carboxylate. Liquid biopsy-informed dosing improved precision for D-methylphenidate only modestly, with greater benefits anticipated in populations exhibiting wider CES1 expression variability (2.8-fold reduction in variability predicted over the CES1 population expression range). Renal function-based individualization fully restored precision and accuracy for oseltamivir carboxylate (1.0-fold relative to reference population exposure), compared with uniform dosing (1.6-fold). The findings underscore that liquid biopsy and conventional physiological markers are complementary tools within a model-informed precision dosing framework, each most valuable when applied to the rate-limiting elimination pathway.

title: Functional dissociation of DDR1 in breast cancer: Kinase-dependent tumor growth and extracellular domain-associated immune regulation.
abstract: Breast cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality in women. Discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1) is a collagen-activated receptor tyrosine kinase with established roles in tumor-matrix signaling. Previous work has shown that the DDR1 extracellular domain (ECD) can contribute to collagen organization and immune exclusion. Here, we asked whether DDR1-associated tumor-intrinsic growth and immune-regulatory phenotypes can be functionally separated in breast cancer models. DDR1 expression and potential immune value were evaluated in three public resources. The public-cohort analyses were not restricted to TNBC, whereas functional validation used the TNBC cell lines MDA-MB-231 and BT-549. DDR1 function was examined using RNA interference, overexpression, CCK-8, BrdU, and Transwell assays. In vivo growth was assessed in MDA-MB-231 and BT-549 NOD/SCID xenografts and in a syngeneic E0771 model in C57BL/6 with persistent Ddr1 suppression. Selected tumor-associated immune-cell populations were recovered using commercial isolation kits and enumerated by cell counting, and E0771 tumors were analyzed by bulk RT-qPCR for selected matrix-remodeling transcripts. DDR1 domain-rescue constructs were used for structure-function analyses. DDR1 was enriched in malignant breast-cancer cells in GSE148673 and showed a significant association with clinical outcome in TCGA-BRCA. After tumor-purity adjustment, DDR1 remained inversely associated with CD8A expression in TCGA-BRCA (R2 = -0.246, P < 0.0001) and GSE22820 (R2 = -0.260, P < 0.0001). RT-qPCR-validated DDR1 knockdown reduced proliferation, DNA synthesis, and invasion in MDA-MB-231 and BT-549 cells, whereas DDR1 overexpression produced reciprocal effects. In the syngeneic E0771 model, persistent Ddr1 suppression reduced tumor growth and was associated with increased recovery of selected tumor-associated immune-cell populations. Domain-rescue experiments were consistent with a partially separable ECD-associated, comparatively kinase-independent immune-regulatory phenotype, but did not formally establish domain sufficiency. These findings support a model in which DDR1 contributes to breast-cancer growth and immune-regulatory phenotypes through partially separable structural features. The clinical datasets support DDR1 as a candidate prognostic and immune-association biomarker, but do not establish independent prognostic value or predictive utility. The immune interpretation is based on selected cell function assay and bulk-tumor transcript measurements and therefore requires deeper phenotypic, functional, and spatial validation. Whether DDR1 or its extracellular domain can be exploited therapeutically remains to be established by direct interventional studies.

title: Ferroptosis-related molecular signatures in Alzheimer's disease and the neuroprotective effects of allicin: an integrated bioinformatics, peripheral single-cell transcriptomic, and experimental study.
abstract: Ferroptosis is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the relationship between AD-associated transcriptomic changes, peripheral immune alterations, and candidate ferroptosis-modulating compounds remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify ferroptosis-related molecular signatures associated with AD and to evaluate whether allicin attenuates ferroptosis-related injury in complementary experimental models. Human hippocampal microarray datasets GSE1297 and GSE28146 were examined with explicit consideration of donor overlap; GSE1297 was treated as the primary subject-level reference dataset, whereas the donor-overlapping GSE28146 dataset was used only as a cross-platform sensitivity source and not as an independent cohort. Ferroptosis-related candidates were prioritized using FerrDb, AD-related annotation, protein-protein interaction analysis, and pathway analysis. Peripheral-blood single-cell RNA-sequencing data (GSE181279) were analyzed to describe immune-cell composition and peripheral distribution of candidate genes without extrapolating these findings to brain-parenchymal cell localization. Candidate-drug prediction and molecular docking were followed by D-galactose/AlCl3 rat experiments and erastin-treated PC12-cell experiments. Histology, ROS, Western blotting, RT-qPCR, and JC-1 assays were used to assess ferroptosis-related molecular and mitochondrial changes. Ferroptosis-focused transcriptomic screening and network prioritization highlighted GPX4, FSP1, SLC7A11, TFRC, and ACSL4 as candidate genes for subsequent analyses. Their expression pattern was compatible with reduced antioxidant defense and increased iron/lipid-peroxidation susceptibility in AD-associated hippocampal transcriptomes. Peripheral single-cell analysis showed heterogeneous expression of these genes across T-cell, B-cell, NK-cell, monocyte, and platelet populations; these results are interpreted as peripheral immune context rather than evidence of brain-cell localization. Molecular docking predicted energetically favorable allicin-protein poses, but does not establish direct target engagement. In the experimental models, allicin attenuated histopathological injury and ROS accumulation, shifted GPX4, FSP1, SLC7A11, TFRC, and ACSL4 expression in an anti-ferroptotic direction, and improved mitochondrial membrane-potential readouts, with changes directionally similar to ferrostatin-1. The combined data support an association between AD-related molecular changes and ferroptosis-regulatory pathways and show that allicin can reduce ferroptosis-related injury in the models used. Because the human datasets include donor overlap, the single-cell dataset is peripheral rather than brain-derived, and direct target-engagement, lipidomic, genetic-rescue, and pharmacokinetic experiments were not performed, the findings should be considered mechanistically suggestive rather than proof that allicin directly targets the five proteins or specifically inhibits AD-associated ferroptosis in humans.

title: Revealing HOXC6 Overexpression and Its Downstream Targets in Small Cell Lung Cancer Through Single-Cell Sequencing-Based Virtual Knockout and CRISPR-Cas9 Analysis.
abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by frequent recurrence and rapid development of therapeutic resistance, underscoring an urgent need to identify stable and reliable molecular biomarkers and actionable therapeutic targets. Homeobox C6 (HOXC6), an important transcription factor of the Homeobox (HOX) family, has not yet been systematically investigated with respect to its expression pattern and biological functions in SCLC. To systematically evaluate differential HOXC6 expression in SCLC; to delineate its cellular origin and functional characteristics at the single-cell level. RNA-seq and microarray data from multiple platforms were integrated to comprehensively analyze HOXC6 mRNA expression, followed by immunohistochemical validation using SCLC and non-SCLC tissue samples from our institution. Quantitative real-time PCR and Transwell migration assays were performed to validate HOXC6 expression and evaluate its effect on the migratory capacity of NCI-H446 cells. SCLC single-cell RNA-sequencing data were analyzed to identify the cellular source of HOXC6, and functional enrichment analyses were performed on genes positively correlated with HOXC6 expression. In silico knockout of HOXC6 was conducted at the single-cell level using scTenifoldKnk, and the predicted transcriptomic alterations were evaluated through differential expression and gene set enrichment analyses. CellChat and scMetabolism were applied to characterize cell-cell communication networks and metabolic pathway activities, respectively. Immune and stromal infiltration patterns were systematically assessed using CIBERSORT, MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, quanTIseq, and ESTIMATE, while immune evasion-related phenotypes were evaluated using TIDE. Finally, ChIP-seq data were integrated with CRISPR dependency screening results for multi-omics cross-validation. Protein-protein molecular docking was subsequently performed to explore potential structural associations of HOXC6 with ACP5 and ZEB2, followed by a 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation of the HOXC6-ACP5 complex to evaluate its predicted conformational stability. Bulk transcriptomic analysis showed that HOXC6 expression was higher in 202 SCLC tissues than in 127 non-SCLC tissues. Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated predominantly nuclear localization of HOXC6 in tumor cells and elevated HOXC6 expression in SCLC. Single-cell analysis revealed that HOXC6 was mainly enriched in neuroendocrine-like cell populations, whereas functional enrichment of HOXC6-positively correlated genes highlighted axonogenesis, microtubule and cytoskeletal organization, and establishment of cell polarity. Following the in silico single-cell knockout of HOXC6, specific transcriptional alterations were computationally predicted, accompanied by enrichment of T-cell proliferation-related pathways. Multi-algorithm immune infiltration analysis further showed that elevated HOXC6 expression was associated with reduced overall immune and stromal signals and cell type-specific remodeling of the tumor microenvironment, although no significant association with the overall TIDE score was observed. In cell-cell communication analyses, the HOXC6-high neuroendocrine-like cell population exhibited hub-like interaction patterns, with the macrophage migration inhibitory factor signaling axis identified as a major communication pathway. Metabolic pathway scoring further indicated that HOXC6 expression was associated with differential activation of glycolysis/gluconeogenesis and oxidative phosphorylation. Integration of ChIP-seq profiles, expression correlations, and CRISPR dependency screening revealed that ACP5 and ZEB2 were generally expressed at low levels in SCLC and were both upregulated following HOXC6 knockout. Enriched HOXC6-binding signals were detected at the ACP5 and ZEB2 loci, and HOXC6 expression was generally negatively correlated with both genes across multiple independent datasets. CRISPR dependency screening additionally indicated that higher ACP5 expression was associated with a suppressive phenotype in SCLC-related cells. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between HOXC6 and ACP5, while the subsequent 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation indicated that the HOXC6-ACP5 complex maintained a relatively stable binding conformation over the simulation period. HOXC6 is overexpressed in SCLC and may contribute to the migratory phenotype of SCLC cells. It may also participate in neuroendocrine-associated transcriptional programs, immunosuppressive features, intercellular communication, and metabolic reprogramming. The integrated regulatory, dependency, molecular-docking, and molecular-dynamics evidence further prioritizes ACP5 as a candidate HOXC6-associated molecule, although the predicted interaction requires direct experimental validation.

title: Emerging trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-targeting antibody-drug conjugates in gynecological cancers.
abstract: Trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP-2) is a transmembrane glycoprotein involved in intracellular signaling pathways that regulate cancer proliferation, invasion, and survival. TROP-2 is minimally expressed in normal tissues but widely overexpressed in epithelial malignancies, including breast, lung, pancreatic, bladder, and gynecologic cancers. Notably, high levels of TROP-2 RNA and protein expression have been reported in endometrial, ovarian, and cervical cancers, supporting its role in tumor progression and its potential value as a therapeutic target. Recent developments have identified TROP-2 as a promising target for antibody-drug conjugates (ADC)s, particularly in advanced or recurrent gynecologic malignancies where therapeutic resistance remains a major clinical challenge. Although immunotherapy, Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors and chemotherapy have shown efficacy in subsets of patients, a significant unmet need persists, especially in those previously treated with platinum-based regimens and immune checkpoint inhibitors. Encouraging preclinical data and early-phase clinical trials have prompted the investigation of several anti-TROP-2 ADCs, including sacituzumab govitecan, datopotamab deruxtecan, and sacituzumab tirumotecan. These agents leverage the selective expression of TROP-2 on tumor cells to deliver cytotoxic payloads, while also demonstrating a bystander effect that extends activity to antigen-negative cells. Their clinical application is currently being explored in gynecologic settings. In this review, we provide an overview of TROP-2's biological role and its relevance as a prognostic and predictive biomarker in gynecologic cancers. We further summarize the available clinical data on TROP-2-targeting ADCs and discuss future perspectives for integrating these agents into therapeutic strategies aimed at improving outcomes in ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers.

title: Radiological and pathological integration predicts the efficacy of bevacizumab with chemotherapy in colorectal cancer liver metastases.
abstract: The differential response of patients with unresectable colorectal cancer liver metastases to bevacizumab plus chemotherapy highlights the urgent need for high-specificity predictive biomarkers. Recent studies suggest that pretreatment contrast-enhanced abdominal CT can noninvasively predict subtypes of liver metastases resistant to bevacizumab-based combination therapy. However, it remains unclear whether integrating intelligent radiological imaging with computational pathology can further enhance predictive performance while simultaneously improving the model's interpretability and elucidating the underlying mechanisms of bevacizumab resistance. Here, we developed a machine learning-based integrative model that combines abdominal CT radiomics with deep learning-based computational pathology to predict the efficacy of bevacizumab combination therapy. Using a multi-center cohort of 319 patients, we allocated patients to the following cohorts: training (n = 120), internal test (n = 50), external test (n = 47), transcriptomic validation (n = 14), and pathological validation (n = 88). The model demonstrated robust predictive performance across all cohorts. Radiomic analysis identified peritumoral features as the most significant contributors. Model interpretation using paired transcriptome data linked therapeutic resistance to inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts. Both deep learning-based histopathological analysis and single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed their pro-angiogenic activity. By integrating features derived from radiographic and histopathological data, we developed a dual-omics model to improve predictive performance and enable efficacy-based stratification. Collectively, our study established an integrative predictive model that combines imaging radiomics and histopathological profiling, thereby elucidating tumor microenvironment heterogeneity associated with therapeutic outcomes. This finding provides practical insights into developing non-invasive biomarkers to characterize the tumor's drug-resistant microenvironment.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identifies PLOD2-Driven Glycolytic Reprogramming in Fibroblasts as a Key Driver of Osteoarthritis Progression.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive joint deterioration. Metabolic imbalance, particularly enhanced glycolytic activity, plays a key role in its pathogenesis. However, previous studies based on bulk transcriptomics have been unable to resolve the specific contributions of different cell types, limiting the in-depth understanding of its molecular mechanisms. This study integrated computational analysis with basic experimental validation. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data (GSE216651) was utilized to systematically analyze cellular heterogeneity and metabolic features in OA joint tissues. Metabolic scoring, pseudotime analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and multiple machine learning algorithms were employed to screen for key glycolysis-related genes. In the experimental section, human fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs) were isolated and treated with LPS or high glucose (HG). PLOD2 was knocked down using siRNA. Techniques including CCK-8 assay, flow cytometry, wound healing assay, Transwell assay, and RT-qPCR were used to assess cell viability, apoptosis, migration, invasion, inflammatory cytokine expression, and glycolysis-related indicators (lactate production, glucose uptake, LDH activity). scRNA-seq analysis revealed that fibroblasts, especially the fibro_PRG4+ subset, exhibited the strongest glycolytic activity in OA, and the proportion of this subset was significantly increased. Multi-omics integration identified six core glycolysis-related genes (AURKA, KIF20A, PLOD2, COL18A1, MLXIPL, GPD1), among which PLOD2 showed the most significant and consistent upregulation. PLOD2 was highly expressed in fibro_PRG4+ fibroblasts, and its expression increased along the pseudotime trajectory of cell differentiation. Experimental validation confirmed elevated PLOD2 expression in FLSs derived from OA patients and in FLSs stimulated by LPS/HG. Knockdown of PLOD2 inhibited FLS activation, migration, invasion, and the release of inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α), while also alleviating chondrocyte injury. Furthermore, both PLOD2 knockdown and treatment with glycolysis inhibitors (Cyto-B, 3BrPA) reversed the HG-induced enhancement of glycolysis (increased lactate production, glucose uptake, LDH activity) and associated inflammatory phenotypes in FLSs. This study reveals significant glycolytic reprogramming in OA fibroblasts, particularly in the fibro_PRG4+ subset, with PLOD2 identified as a key regulatory molecule involved in synovial cell activation, inflammatory response, and cartilage damage. These findings elucidate the role of cell-type-specific metabolic alterations in OA progression and suggest that targeting PLOD2 and the glycolytic pathway may offer novel strategies for OA intervention.

title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Reveals a Pan-Cancer Treg Cell Signature Associated With Immunotherapy Resistance.
abstract: Regulatory T (Treg) cells contribute to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICIs) resistance in cancer, yet a systematic approach to capture their pan-cancer impact on treatment outcomes remains limited. We analyzed scRNA-seq data from ICI-treated patients to characterize Treg-related features, including patient-level Treg proportions and exploratory intra-Treg CIBERSORTx scores. Treg.Sig, a pan-cancer Treg-associated immune-microenvironmental signature, was then derived from pre-annotated Treg cells across 32 scRNA-seq datasets and further evaluated by patient-level pseudobulk sensitivity analyses. The signature's association with immunosuppression, intratumor heterogeneity (ITH), and total mutation burden (TMB) was assessed in the TCGA pan-cancer cohort. Building upon this signature, we applied and systematically compared seven machine learning and four deep learning algorithms across 10 ICIs-treated RNA-Seq cohorts to identify the optimal predictive model. Finally, 29 CRISPR datasets were analyzed to prioritize resistance-associated targets, with candidate genes validated by immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blot. Exploratory cell-level analyses showed lower intra-Treg CIBERSORTx scores in responders in both cohorts. In SKCM, patient-level analysis showed a higher Treg/CD4 T-cell proportion in non-responders, whereas broader Treg proportions did not differ by response. Treg.Sig was positively correlated with markers of immunosuppression, ITH, and TMB. The optimal Treg.Sig model achieved area under the receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curves (AUCs) of 0.74 and 0.72 in validation and test sets, respectively, and 0.61-0.87 in independent test sets, outperforming existing transcriptomic models in predicting ICIs response. Among Treg.Sig genes, five immune resistance-related genes were identified through CRISPR data; LYZ and C1QA were significantly downregulated in ICIs responders, as confirmed by multiple experimental approaches. We developed a pan-cancer Treg-associated immune-microenvironmental signature and, through systematic application of multiple machine-learning and deep-learning algorithms, established a predictive model for ICI-response stratification. These findings support the potential utility of Treg.Sig for treatment-response stratification and highlight candidate genes for further investigation in Treg-associated immune resistance.

title: HDAC1 inhibits CDX2 expression and promotes colorectal cancer cell migration.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common and second deadliest cancer worldwide. The transcription factor caudal type homeobox 2 (CDX2) is essential for intestinal development and epithelial homeostasis and serves as a prognostic marker in CRC. Its loss is associated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition, metastasis, and poor prognosis in CRC. Interestingly, CDX2 is rarely mutated (0.9% allele mutation frequency), suggesting that epigenetic mechanisms contribute to its downregulation. Using a combination of pharmacological screening and genetic approaches in 2D and physiologically relevant 3D culture systems, we identified HDAC1 as a potent transcriptional repressor of CDX2. ChIP-qPCR detected HDAC1 occupancy at a CDX2 promoter region and increased H3K27 acetylation at this region following Quisinostat treatment, supporting this region as the strongest HDAC1-associated regulatory region under the experimental conditions used. Quisinostat restored CDX2 expression by up to 4-fold in CRC cells cultured in both 2D and 3D systems. Moreover, both genetic silencing of HDAC1 and pharmacological HDAC inhibition with Quisinostat significantly reduced CRC cell migration (p ≤ 0.01, nonparametric Mann-Whitney U test), concomitant with increased CDX2 expression. Analysis of publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data from CRC patients revealed an inverse association between HDAC1 and CDX2 expression in epithelial tumor cells. Together, our findings identify HDAC1 as an epigenetic regulator of CDX2 expression and show that HDAC1 targeting is accompanied by reduced CRC cell migration. Further mechanistic studies are required to define the contribution of CDX2 to the anti-migratory effects of HDAC1 inhibition, while validation in independent clinical CRC cohorts is needed to confirm the HDAC1-CDX2 relationship at the protein level and establish its prognostic relevance.
